# LUZ

> Install LUZ, find a component and copy its markup, or look up a token, a page pattern or an HTML element. MIT licence. In beta: any release may break anything, and the changelog says how to migrate.

Packages, in load order: @luz-ds/tokens, @luz-ds/core, @luz-ds/site, then one for your kind of site (@luz-ds/landing, @luz-ds/cms or @luz-ds/app). Use only the classes listed in each package's classes.json. After you write HTML or CSS, run `npx @luz-ds/check` on the files and fix what it reports; it reads source, so it does not replace testing in a browser.

One entry per page of the documentation, in reading order. The markup of an entry shows its classes and elements; the `classes.json` of each package lists them all.

## Install LUZ
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/

Pick a level, then copy one install command or the CDN tags. Each level needs the ones below it and nothing above.

Know what you are building? [Choose your snippet](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/snippet/) and copy the lines for it, CDN hashes included.

Beta

Names, classes and behaviour can still change before the stable release. Pin an exact version, and read the changelog before you upgrade.

### Which level do I need?

- **Your own components, LUZ's colours and spacing:** level 1, tokens only.
- **Ready-made buttons, forms, tables and dialogs:** level 2, tokens and core.
- **Whole pages: shell, page header, footer, search:** level 3, all three packages.
- **A landing page, with its header, hero and blocks:** level 3 and [a package for that kind of site](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/#site-kinds).

### Level 1: tokens only

CSS custom properties: the colour, space and type scales, and the colours of light, dark and high contrast. No other LUZ package is needed.

`pnpm add @luz-ds/tokens`

CDN tags, level 1
```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/tokens@0.0.0/dist/luz-tokens.min.css">
```

With a bundler such as Vite, import the files instead of adding tags. A `href` cannot name a package: these paths are for `import` only.

Bundler imports, level 1
```js
import "@luz-ds/tokens/css";
```

- Running text and headings use ET Book, an MIT-licensed font that ships with the tokens. Controls, labels and tables use the system sans, and code the system mono.
- Bringing your own fonts? Load `dist/tokens.min.css` instead: the same tokens without any `@font-face`.
- Check your own colours against the WCAG ratios with `npx @luz-ds/tokens check-contrast`, or [in the browser](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/contrast/).

### Level 2: tokens and core

The 32 components, the styles of bare HTML elements, and optional JavaScript. Load tokens first.

`pnpm add @luz-ds/tokens @luz-ds/core`

CDN tags, level 2
```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/tokens@0.0.0/dist/luz-tokens.min.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/core@0.0.0/dist/luz.min.css">

<!-- Optional: copy buttons, tabs, players, the color mode -->
<script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/core@0.0.0/dist/luz.min.js"></script>
```

Bundler imports, level 2
```js
import "@luz-ds/tokens/css";
import "@luz-ds/core/css";

// Optional: copy buttons, tabs, players, the color mode
import "@luz-ds/core";
```

- Every page works without the script. See [what each JavaScript module adds](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/javascript/).
- Need a single component? Load `dist/base.min.css` plus the file you want, for example `dist/components/button.min.css`.
- Markup you cannot add classes to, such as Markdown or a CMS? Load [`classless.css`](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/classless/) and mark the zone with `data-luz-classless`.

### Level 3: tokens, core and site

Six components that need data of the site: search, cookie consent, color mode, language switch, submenu and banner. Site needs core and tokens. The page structure, from the header to the footer, is in landing and cms, which work without site.

`pnpm add @luz-ds/tokens @luz-ds/core @luz-ds/site`

CDN tags, level 3
```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/tokens@0.0.0/dist/luz-tokens.min.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/core@0.0.0/dist/luz.min.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/site@0.0.0/dist/site.min.css">

<!-- Optional: core behaviours, and the site search and cookie banner -->
<script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/core@0.0.0/dist/luz.min.js"></script>
<script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/site@0.0.0/dist/site.min.js"></script>
```

Bundler imports, level 3
```js
import "@luz-ds/tokens/css";
import "@luz-ds/core/css";
import "@luz-ds/site/css";

// Optional: core behaviours, and the site search
import "@luz-ds/core";
import "@luz-ds/site";
```

### Packages for one kind of site

On top of level 3, a package can add what one kind of site needs: [Landing](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/landing/), the header, hero, sections and footer of a landing page and blocks to copy for it, [CMS](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/cms/), the header, page header, article header, table of contents and footer of a blog or a newspaper, with any CMS, and [App](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/app/), the header and the dashboard of a web application. Each needs the packages of level 2, loaded first; site is optional for them, and the commands below add it for its search and its language switch. Install the one you need.

`pnpm add @luz-ds/tokens @luz-ds/core @luz-ds/site @luz-ds/landing`

CDN tags, landing
```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/tokens@0.0.0/dist/luz-tokens.min.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/core@0.0.0/dist/luz.min.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/site@0.0.0/dist/site.min.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/landing@0.0.0/dist/landing.min.css">

<!-- Optional: core behaviours, and the site search and cookie banner -->
<script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/core@0.0.0/dist/luz.min.js"></script>
<script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/site@0.0.0/dist/site.min.js"></script>
```

`pnpm add @luz-ds/tokens @luz-ds/core @luz-ds/site @luz-ds/cms`

CDN tags, cms
```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/tokens@0.0.0/dist/luz-tokens.min.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/core@0.0.0/dist/luz.min.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/site@0.0.0/dist/site.min.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/cms@0.0.0/dist/cms.min.css">

<!-- Optional: core behaviours, and the site search and cookie banner -->
<script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/core@0.0.0/dist/luz.min.js"></script>
<script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/site@0.0.0/dist/site.min.js"></script>
```

`pnpm add @luz-ds/tokens @luz-ds/core @luz-ds/site @luz-ds/app`

CDN tags, app
```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/tokens@0.0.0/dist/luz-tokens.min.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/core@0.0.0/dist/luz.min.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/site@0.0.0/dist/site.min.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/app@0.0.0/dist/app.min.css">

<!-- Optional: core behaviours, and the site search and cookie banner -->
<script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/core@0.0.0/dist/luz.min.js"></script>
<script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/site@0.0.0/dist/site.min.js"></script>
```

- Landing, cms and app each have their own version and need `^0.1.0` of the base. Pin both numbers.
- With a bundler, add `import "@luz-ds/landing/css";`, `import "@luz-ds/cms/css";` or `import "@luz-ds/app/css";` after the imports of level 3.
- None has a script. Core's script is optional: with cms, it marks the section in view in the table of contents; with app, it marks the current link of the sidebar and closes the drawer when a link is followed.

### Before you ship

- npm and pnpm install the lower levels for you. Yarn only warns, so list every package, as above.
- On a CDN, pin an exact version and add an `integrity` hash with `crossorigin="anonymous"`. Compute the hash from the file you load, as below.
- The core and site scripts warn in the console when the level below is missing.
- Set `lang` on `<html>`: core's scripts write their text in that language (English and Spanish ship).

Computing the integrity hash
```text
curl -s https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/core@0.0.0/dist/luz.min.css | openssl dgst -sha384 -binary | openssl base64 -A
```

Write the result as `integrity="sha384-…"` on the tag that loads that file, and repeat it for each file.

A hash on a script covers that file only, not the files it loads later. `site.min.js` loads `search.min.js` on a page with a search and `consent.min.js` on a page with a cookie banner and `mode.min.js` on a page with an Auto color mode. Give each one its own hash in an import map, before the first module script. It works in Chrome 127, Safari 18 and Firefox 138 and later; an older browser ignores it and loads the files unchecked. A `<link rel="modulepreload">` with a hash is not a guard in Safari or Firefox: use it as a performance hint only.

Integrity for the site scripts
```html
<script type="importmap">
{
  "integrity": {
    "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/site@0.0.0/dist/search.min.js": "sha384-…",
    "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/site@0.0.0/dist/consent.min.js": "sha384-…",
    "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/site@0.0.0/dist/mode.min.js": "sha384-…"
  }
}
</script>
<script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/site@0.0.0/dist/site.min.js" integrity="sha384-…" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
```

### Next steps

- [Choose your snippet](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/snippet/) for your kind of site and the way you load it.
- [Browse the components](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/) and copy their markup.
- [Set up the color modes](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/modes/): light, dark and high contrast.
- [Learn how the tokens work](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/) before you write your own components.
- [See how LUZ is organised](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/structure/): packages, CSS layers and the page skeleton.

## Choose your snippet
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/snippet/

Pick what you are building and how you load it, then copy the lines. The CDN lines carry integrity hashes computed from the published files.

Every snippet loads tokens first, then core, then the package for your kind of site, in the order the [cascade layers](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/layers/) expect. The site package is optional for a landing page, a blog and an application, so its lines are marked and safe to delete. For the level-by-level explanation, read [Install LUZ](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/); for a build tool, [With a bundler or framework](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/bundler/).

## How LUZ is organised
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/structure/

Packages that depend in one direction, CSS in cascade layers inside one called luz, and one optional script.

### Package boundaries

Each package depends on the ones above it in this list, never on the ones below.

The name stands for Light, Usable & Zero-dependency: light in weight (plain CSS and ES modules, nothing to build for the people who use it), usable by everyone (native HTML, three color modes, tested for accessibility), and with zero runtime dependencies.

Package dependency chain
```text
@luz-ds/tokens   -> primitive and semantic tokens (standalone)
      ↓ required by
@luz-ds/core     -> components, objects, bare-element styles, optional JS
      ↓ required by
@luz-ds/site     -> search, consent, mode, lang-switch, submenu and banner

Each of these needs tokens and core, and takes site as an optional peer:
@luz-ds/landing  -> header, hero, sections and footer of a landing page (own version, 0.x)
@luz-ds/cms      -> page structure of a blog, a newspaper or any CMS (own version, 0.x)
@luz-ds/app      -> header and dashboard of a web application (own version, 0.x)
```

- Landing, cms and app need tokens and core, and can use site when you load it, never each other; site needs core and tokens; core needs tokens; tokens needs nothing.
- Tokens, core and site share one version. A package for one kind of site, such as landing, cms or app, has its own, and names the major of the others it needs.
- The packages say so as peer dependencies: required for tokens and core, optional for site in landing, cms and app. The core and site scripts warn in the console when a level is missing.

### What each package needs

Find the part you want, and install the package of its row and the ones below it.

Which package holds each part of a page

- Color modes, semantic tokens, ET Book: `--luz-*`, `data-theme`: tokens: Nothing else is needed
- Reset and styles of bare HTML elements: `h1`, `p`, `a`, `ul`…: core: In `base.css` and `luz.css`
- Components: `.luz-btn`, `.luz-field`, `.luz-card`, `.luz-table`, `.luz-tabs`…: core: Also one file each, in `components/`
- Modal: `.luz-modal` on a `<dialog>`: core: The script is a fallback for browsers without `command` and `commandfor`
- Layout objects: `.o-container`, `.o-grid`, `.o-stack`, `.o-media`: core: Spacing comes from the space tokens
- An app layout with a sidebar: `.o-shell`, `.o-main`, `.luz-sidebar`: core: A plain `<footer>` as a direct child of `.o-shell` goes across the bottom; its look is yours, or a kind of site's footer
- A page with no sidebar, a sticky bar, an action group: `.o-page`, `.o-sticky`, `.o-actions`: core: Instead of `.o-shell`, for a page with no sidebar: [the page and its bars](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/layout/#objects-page)
- Skip link, band, image frame: `.luz-skip-link`, `.luz-band`, `.luz-image`: core: The image frame keeps a ratio and crops the picture to it; with no picture it is a flat surface
- The header, hero, sections and footer of a landing page: `.luz-landing-header`, `-hero`, `-main`, `-section`, `-footer`, `-glow`: landing: On core's objects (`.o-page`, `.o-sticky`, `.o-container`, `.o-grid--split`) and core's navbar; site is optional. A feature grid is `ul.o-grid.o-grid--split`, core's
- The header, page header, article header, table of contents and footer of a blog or a newspaper: `.luz-cms-header` (`--masthead`), `-page-header`, `-article-header`, `-article`, `-toc`, `-footer`: cms: On core's objects and navbar; site is optional. Post cards, listings and the author box are core's card: [CMS templates](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/cms/templates/)
- The header and the dashboard of a web application: `.luz-app-header` (`__product`, `__actions`, `__account`), `.luz-app-dashboard` (`__head`, `__title`, `__panel`): app: On core's shell, sidebar, sticky bar, grid and card; site is optional, for the search. No script. See [App](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/app/)
- The links of a header, and its menu button: `.luz-navbar`, `.luz-nav-toggle`: core: A popover panel at 768 px and below, with no script
- Submenu, banner: `<luz-submenu>`, `<luz-banner>`: site: Tags with no script and no class: the submenu is a native `<details>` in a header's links, the banner a `<section>`
- Cookie consent: `<luz-consent>`, `.luz-consent`: site: `site.js` loads its script, `consent.js`, when the page has one; a band fixed at the bottom of the window; without the script it stays hidden
- Auto color mode: `<luz-mode>`: site: `site.js` loads its script, `mode.js`, when the page has one; without it the radios of core's switcher still work and Auto is light
- Language switch: `<luz-lang-switch>`: site: No script
- Site search: `<luz-search>`, `.luz-search`: site: Needs the script (`site.js`, which loads `search.js` when the page has one) and an index file; without them it is a link
- Print styles: Nothing to add: core: In `luz.css`; site adds its own print rules
- Markup you cannot add classes to: `data-luz-classless`: core: `classless.css`, a file of its own
- Checking what you or an AI agent wrote: `npx @luz-ds/check`, the `luz-check` command: check: A tool with no CSS and no layer, and no other package needed: it reads your HTML and CSS offline. See [Working with AI](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/ai/)

- **Two ways to lay out a page, both core's.** `.o-shell` with `.o-main`: a sidebar column beside the main area. `.o-page`: a header, the content and a footer in one column. Pick one for the grid of the page: the first when it has a sidebar, the second when it has none. A landing or CMS header and footer work with both; these docs use `.o-shell`.
- Site needs core, and core needs tokens, so a row at a level also needs every package under it. Landing, CMS and app need core and tokens; site is optional for them.

### CSS layers

Core's CSS comes in native cascade layers (`@layer`), in ITCSS order, inside one container layer called `luz`. The six below are the ones that hold its rules; [the layers page](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/layers/) lists them all, with tokens, site and print. A later layer wins over an earlier one, and any CSS of yours that is not in a layer wins over all of LUZ, with no `!important`. [How to order and override them](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/layers/).

Core cascade layers
```text
packages/core/src/
  settings/_settings.css      luz.settings    motion, z-index, breakpoints
  generic/_reset.css          luz.generic     the reset
  elements/*.css              luz.elements    bare HTML elements, zero specificity
  objects/_objects.css        luz.objects     layout: .o-*
  components/*.css            luz.components  the components: .luz-*
  utilities/_utilities.css    luz.utilities   single-purpose helpers: .u-*
```

- The components layer holds 32 components.
- `dist/luz.css` holds these six layers and `luz.print`. Tokens are in `luz.tokens`, site in `luz.site`, landing in `luz.landing`, cms in `luz.cms` and app in `luz.app`; `luz.themes` is empty, kept for a look of your own. For a page that needs a few components only, load `dist/base.css` (settings, reset and elements), then `dist/components/<name>.css` for each one.
- Rules for bare elements are wrapped in `:where()`, so any class wins over them.

### The script

One optional entry point, `luz.js`, starts every behaviour on the page: color mode, copy buttons, dialogs, highlighting, players, tabs and the sidebar.

Load the core script
```html
<script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/core@0.1.0/dist/luz.min.js"></script>
```

To load less, import one module and call its `init` function. See [JavaScript modules](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/javascript/).

### Minimal page

Minimal page skeleton
```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en" data-theme="light">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>Sign up – Acme</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/tokens@0.1.0/dist/luz-tokens.min.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/core@0.1.0/dist/luz.min.css">
</head>
<body>
  <main class="o-container">
    <h1>Sign up</h1>
    <form action="/signup/" method="post">
      <div class="luz-field">
        <label class="luz-field__label" for="email">Email</label>
        <input class="luz-input" id="email" name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email" required>
      </div>
      <button class="luz-btn luz-btn--primary" type="submit">Create account</button>
    </form>
  </main>
</body>
</html>
```

## How to read LUZ
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/how-to-read/

What the names in LUZ's CSS, markup and tokens tell you, and which of them you can rely on.

### Class names

The start of a class name tells you what it is and which package it comes from.

What each class prefix means

- `.luz-`: A component, or a part of one: core: `.luz-btn`
- `.o-`: A layout object: it arranges things and has no look of its own: core: `.o-stack`
- `.u-`: A utility: one job, with no component around it: core: `.u-sr-only`
- `.luz-landing-`: A piece of a landing page: landing: `.luz-landing-hero`
- `.luz-cms-`: A piece of a blog, a newspaper or any CMS: cms: `.luz-cms-header`
- `.luz-app-`: A piece of a web application: app: `.luz-app-header`
- `.is-`: A state a script mirrors onto an element. Read it, but do not style from outside: it is not part of what you can rely on: core: `.is-active`

Inside a component, two separators say how the pieces fit. A double underscore names a part of the component: `.luz-card__title` is the title of a card. A double hyphen names a variant of it: `.luz-btn--primary` is the primary button.

Read this markup from left to right, one class at a time.

A card with a primary button
```html
<div class="o-stack">
  <article class="luz-card">
    <h3 class="luz-card__title">Team plan</h3>
    <button class="luz-btn luz-btn--primary" type="button">Choose plan</button>
  </article>
</div>
```

- `o-stack` is a layout object: it spaces its children in a column.
- `luz-card` is a component, a card.
- `luz-card__title` is a part of the card: its title.
- `luz-btn` is another component, a button, and `luz-btn--primary` is its primary variant.

### Token names

A token is a CSS custom property that starts with `--luz-`. The next word says what kind of value it holds.

One token of each kind

- `--luz-blue-60`: Primitive: A raw color: a family and a step. It has no role and never changes with the mode
- `--luz-brand-primary`: Semantic token: A role: the color of links and actions. It has a value for each mode
- `--luz-space-md`: Scale step: One step of the space scale
- `--luz-text-lg`: Scale step: One step of the type scale
- `--luz-type-base`: Knob: The value a whole scale is worked out from. Change it to resize every step
- `--luz-z-modal`: Setting: A value core uses to lay out the page: stacking order, motion and breakpoints

- LUZ's own components read semantic tokens and scale steps. They never read a primitive or a knob.
- You can set any token in your own CSS. [Make it yours](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/make-it-yours/) shows how.

Each family has a page: [color](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/color/), [typography](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/typography/), [spacing and sizing](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/spacing/), [radius](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/radius/), [shadows](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/shadows/), [motion](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/motion/) and [layout and breakpoints](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/layout/).

### Attributes

Classes are for style. Attributes that start with `data-` are how a script and your markup talk to each other.

- `data-theme` on `<html>` picks the color mode (`light`, `dark` or `high-contrast`) or the name of a look of your own.
- `data-mode` on `<html>` picks the color mode inside a look of your own: `data-theme="my-brand"` with `data-mode="dark"`.
- `data-luz-*` are the hooks of LUZ's scripts, such as `data-luz-js`, which the script sets on `<html>` once it runs. A script binds to these, never to a class.
- `data-luz-classless` turns on [classless styles](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/classless/) for the markup inside it.
- `data-luz-label-*` overrides one string a script writes.

These are examples, not the full list: each component's page names the attributes it uses.

### Elements that start with luz

A tag that starts with `luz-` is a custom element. LUZ's are in the light DOM, so your CSS reaches inside them, and their parts are classes: `.luz-<tag>__<part>`.

- **With a script:** `<luz-search>`, `<luz-consent>`, `<luz-mode>` and `<luz-timeline>` need their script to do their job.
- **CSS only:** `<luz-lang-switch>`, `<luz-submenu>` and `<luz-banner>` have no script at all. They are a tag you can style before and without its script.

Which package holds each one is in [How LUZ is organised](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/structure/).

### Layers, in one paragraph

All of LUZ's CSS is in one cascade layer called `luz`, with named layers inside it, and any CSS of yours that is not in a layer wins over all of it, with no `!important`. [Cascade layers](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/layers/) lists them in order and shows how to override one.

### What you can rely on

Not every name is a promise. These four parts of LUZ are public API: a change to them is announced.

- **Tokens**: every `--luz-` custom property in `tokens.css`, not the ones a component declares for itself.
- **Classes**: `.luz-`, `.o-` and `.u-` classes in the markup the docs show, with their parts and variants. Not `.is-` classes.
- **Attributes**: `data-theme`, `data-mode`, `data-luz-*` and `data-luz-label-*`. Not the attributes the docs site's own scripts use.
- **Packages**: the `exports` map of each package and the paths of the files it publishes.

In beta, anything may break, and the changeset of the release says how to migrate. Read [What is public API, in VERSIONING.md on GitHub](https://github.com/nandovejer/luz/blob/main/VERSIONING.md) for the whole table.

### Reading a file name

A file name says what is in it. Every CSS file also has a `.min` twin that holds the same rules, minified: `luz.css` and `luz.min.css`.

Files in the dist folder of each package

- `luz-tokens.css`: `@luz-ds/tokens`: Always, unless you bring your own font. It has the tokens and the `@font-face` rules of ET Book
- `tokens.css`: `@luz-ds/tokens`: Instead of `luz-tokens.css`, when you bring your own font: the same tokens, with no `@font-face`
- `luz.css`: `@luz-ds/core`: For the reset, the bare elements, the layout objects, the components and the utilities, all at once
- `base.css`: `@luz-ds/core`: When you want only a few components: the reset and the bare elements, then one file per component
- `components/<name>.css`: `@luz-ds/core`: After `base.css`, for each component you use
- `classless.css`: `@luz-ds/core`: For markup you cannot add classes to, inside `data-luz-classless`. It is a file of its own, not in `luz.css`
- `themes/_template.css`: `@luz-ds/core`: Never as it is: copy it as the start of a look of your own
- `site.css`: `@luz-ds/site`: When the page uses a site element such as `<luz-search>`

To pick the lines for your build, [choose your snippet](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/snippet/).

## Make it yours
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/make-it-yours/

Change the colours, fonts, sizes, corners and shadows of LUZ with tokens, and adjust one component with CSS of your own.

LUZ is made to be changed from the outside. You do not edit its files: you write CSS of your own that loads after it, and the rule that matters is that your CSS wins.

### Change a token, not a component

LUZ's components read tokens: custom properties that start with `--luz-`. To change how LUZ looks, write the token again in your own CSS. Every component that reads it follows.

The token override
```css
:root {
  --luz-radius-md: 2px;
}
```

- Write the token on `:root`, in CSS that is not inside an `@layer`.
- CSS outside any layer wins over every LUZ layer, wherever it sits in the file. You do not need `!important`, or a longer selector.
- If you use layers of your own, declare their order first. [Cascade layers](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/layers/) has the order and the three ways to override LUZ.
- Token names are on [the Tokens pages](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/). A token you write that LUZ does not read does nothing.

### Colours and modes

LUZ ships one look in three modes: light, dark and high contrast. Colours are semantic tokens, such as `--luz-brand-fill` and `--luz-surface-page`, and each one has a value for each mode. To change them, [make your own theme](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/themes/): it gives you a template, the steps and where to load it. Then run [the contrast check](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/contrast/) on your colours, which measures the pairs LUZ promises to keep readable.

### Fonts

Two tokens say which font is used for what. Three more hold the font stacks.

- `--luz-font-body`: running text. The serif, ET Book, by default.
- `--luz-font-heading`: headings. The serif by default.
- `--luz-font-sans`, `--luz-font-serif` and `--luz-font-mono`: the three stacks. Controls, labels and tables use the sans, and code uses the mono.

The font override
```css
@font-face {
  font-family: "My Serif";
  src: url("/fonts/my-serif.woff2") format("woff2");
  font-display: swap;
}

:root {
  --luz-font-serif: "My Serif", georgia, serif;
}
```

- Your own `@font-face` goes in your CSS, as above. Setting `--luz-font-serif` changes the body and the headings, because both use it by default.
- To drop ET Book, load `tokens.css` instead of `luz-tokens.css`: `@luz-ds/tokens/tokens.css` from a bundler, `dist/tokens.min.css` from a CDN. It has the same tokens and no `@font-face`.
- On an element marked `lang="ar"`, body and headings already take the sans: ET Book has no Arabic letters. A rule of your own, outside LUZ's layers, still wins.
- A font you bring has its own licence. Read it before you publish the file.

[Typography](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/typography/) lists the font roles and the type scale.

### Text and space sizes

Three tokens, called knobs, set the size of the whole type scale and the whole space scale. Every type step, `--luz-text-xs` to `--luz-text-4xl`, and every space step, `--luz-space-3xs` to `--luz-space-4xl`, is worked out from them, so one line changes the page.

The three size knobs

- `--luz-type-base`: 1rem: The size of `--luz-text-base`. Every other step is computed from it.
- `--luz-type-ratio`: 1.25: The multiple between two steps above the base, and the divisor below it.
- `--luz-space-unit`: 0.25rem: The grid of the spacing scale: every space step is a multiple of it.

The size knobs
```css
:root {
  --luz-type-base: 1.125rem;
  --luz-type-ratio: 1.2;
  --luz-space-unit: 0.1875rem;
}
```

#### Rules for the knobs

- **Write lengths in rem.** A rem follows the font size the reader chose in their browser settings. A value in px pins the size and ignores that setting. Spacing is in rem too, so it grows with the text.
- **Set them on `:root`.** The steps are worked out once, on `:root`, and passed down as finished values. A knob on `body` or on a section changes nothing. Sizes are a choice for the whole page.

A knob that does nothing
```css
/* This changes nothing: the steps are already worked out on :root */
body {
  --luz-type-base: 1.5rem;
}
```

#### The ranges LUZ is tested at

- `--luz-type-base`: 0.875rem to 1.25rem.
- `--luz-type-ratio`: 1.125 to 1.5.
- `--luz-space-unit`: 0.1875rem to 0.3125rem, which is 3px to 5px at a 16px root.

Outside these ranges it still works, but nobody has looked at the result. The colour contrast check measures colours only: it does not look at sizes.

#### What does not move

- Small text keeps a floor. `--luz-text-xs` is never under 0.75rem and `--luz-text-sm` never under 0.875rem, whatever the base.
- On a touch screen, and at 768px and below, form text is never under 1rem.
- Control heights, `--luz-control-sm` to `--luz-control-xl` (28, 36, 44 and 56px), are not knobs. A smaller unit never makes a target smaller.
- Running text is `--luz-text-body`, 1.0625 times the base, so the base moves it too.

#### By width, or on paper

The knobs are on `:root`, so a media query can change them.

Knobs in media queries
```css
@media (min-width: 80em) {
  :root {
    --luz-type-base: 1.125rem;
  }
}

@media print {
  :root {
    --luz-type-base: 0.9375rem;
  }
}
```

#### Try them

These are the nine type sizes of five combinations of the knobs. The steps are `--luz-text-xs` to `--luz-text-4xl`, in px.

Type sizes at 16px root

- Default: 12: 14: 15: 16: 20: 25: 31: 39: 49
- Larger text `--luz-type-base: 1.125rem`: 12: 14: 16: 18: 23: 29: 36: 45: 56
- Tighter steps `--luz-type-ratio: 1.2`: 12: 14: 15: 16: 19: 23: 28: 34: 41
- Small base `--luz-type-base: 0.875rem`: 12: 14: 14: 14: 18: 23: 29: 36: 45
- Large and wide `--luz-type-base: 1.25rem; --luz-type-ratio: 1.333`: 12: 15: 18: 20: 27: 36: 48: 64: 85

- The table is for a root font size of 16px, the browser default. If the reader's browser is set to 20px, every size is 1.25 times larger. That is why the knobs are in rem.
- With a base of 0.875rem the floors hold: `--luz-text-sm`, `--luz-text-md` and `--luz-text-base` are all 14px.
- Each step is rounded to 1/16 rem, which is a whole pixel at a 16px root. A browser without `round()` uses the plain chain: at the defaults the three largest steps are at most 0.25px away.

[Typography](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/typography/) and [Spacing and sizing](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/spacing/) list each step with its formula.

### Corners

`--luz-radius-md` is the ceiling: no rectangle is rounder. It is the corner of buttons, cards, alerts, menus and dialogs. Three more steps cover the other cases.

- `--luz-radius-none` (0px): a square corner, for a box that joins a neighbour.
- `--luz-radius-sm` (2px): small marks, such as inline code and a checkbox.
- `--luz-radius-full` (9999px): a pill or a circle, for shapes that are round by nature. It is not a corner for a box.

Square corners
```css
:root {
  --luz-radius-sm: 0;
  --luz-radius-md: 0;
}
```

[Radius](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/radius/) says which component uses which step.

### Shadows

Three tokens set how far a surface seems to float: `--luz-shadow-sm` for a card, `--luz-shadow-md` for tooltips and toasts, and `--luz-shadow-lg` for dialogs and the drawer.

LUZ redraws them in dark mode, and in high contrast it draws outlines instead. A rule on `:root` outside any layer wins in every mode, so one value serves them all. If you want the dark ones heavier, set them for that mode as well.

Shadows for light and dark
```css
:root {
  --luz-shadow-md: 0 2px 6px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.12);
}

[data-theme="dark"] {
  --luz-shadow-md: 0 4px 12px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6);
}
```

Never let a shadow be the only edge of a surface: it disappears in forced colors. [Shadows](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/shadows/) has the values, and [Color modes](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/modes/) how the three modes are chosen.

### Adjust one component

Change a token first: every component that reads it follows, in every mode. When one component needs a rule of its own, write it in CSS outside any layer. It wins over every LUZ layer, so the selector can stay short.

A rule for one component
```css
.luz-btn {
  min-height: 3rem;
}
```

If your own CSS is in layers, declare the order first and put the rule in your layer. `app` comes after `luz`, so it wins.

Your own layers
```css
@layer reset, luz, app;

@layer app {
  .luz-btn {
    min-height: 3rem;
  }
}
```

Three things to avoid.

- **`!important`.** It is never needed: unlayered CSS and the order of layers decide first.
- **A status colour for something else.** Success, warning, danger and info keep their meaning, so do not use them to decorate.
- **Removing the focus ring.** `outline: none` leaves a keyboard user with no way to see where they are. Change its colour with `--luz-focus-ring` and check the result with [the contrast check](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/contrast/).

[Cascade layers](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/layers/) has the full order of LUZ's layers.

### Icons

LUZ draws 22 icons of its own, on [the Icon grid page](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/icon-grid/), which also has the markup. For hundreds, bring a set. Whatever set you use, the pattern is the same:

1. Use an inline `<svg>` that takes `currentColor`. It follows the text colour and the mode, and it works in forced colors.
2. Mark it decorative with `aria-hidden="true"` and `focusable="false"`. Its name comes from the visible text beside it, or from a `.u-sr-only` span in the button.
3. Size it in em, such as `1.25em`, so it follows the text and the size knobs. There is no icon-size token on purpose. Inside `.luz-btn` an icon is 16px already.
4. Draw one icon many times from one `<symbol>` sprite in the same document, never `<use href="https://…">`, which browsers block across origins.
5. An icon never carries meaning alone: a status icon comes with words. Do not use a set's brand logos as a status or an action. They are trademarks, even where the set is MIT.

An icon beside a label
```html
<button class="luz-btn luz-btn--secondary" type="button">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="1.25em" height="1.25em" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false">
    <use href="#icon-download"></use>
  </svg>
  Download
</button>
```

#### Sets with an MIT licence

These five are under the MIT licence only, the licence LUZ itself uses. Each licence file was read on 2026-10-15.

Icon sets under the MIT licence

- [Feather](https://github.com/feathericons/feather): MIT: [Feather licence file](https://github.com/feathericons/feather/blob/HEAD/LICENSE): A 24px grid and a 2px stroke, like LUZ's own icons. Check how recently the repository was updated before you choose it.
- [Heroicons](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/heroicons): MIT: [Heroicons licence file](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/heroicons/blob/HEAD/LICENSE): Outline icons at 24px, solid icons at 24, 20 and 16px.
- [Tabler Icons](https://github.com/tabler/tabler-icons): MIT: [Tabler Icons licence file](https://github.com/tabler/tabler-icons/blob/HEAD/LICENSE): A very large set. The stroke width can be changed; it is 2px by default.
- [Phosphor](https://github.com/phosphor-icons/core): MIT: [Phosphor licence file](https://github.com/phosphor-icons/core/blob/HEAD/LICENSE): Six weights. Take one, so the icons match.
- [Bootstrap Icons](https://github.com/twbs/icons): MIT: [Bootstrap Icons licence file](https://github.com/twbs/icons/blob/HEAD/LICENSE): A 16px grid.

Iconoir, Ionicons, Radix Icons and Fluent UI System Icons are also under MIT, as of 2026-10-15. They are not on this list to keep it short.

LUZ does not bundle these and does not test them. MIT asks you to keep the copyright notice: copy the notice of the set you take next to its icons, and check the licence file of the version you take.

#### Sets LUZ does not recommend

These are popular, and each has a licence that is not MIT only. The reason is listed so nobody adds them by mistake.

Icon sets that are not MIT only

- Lucide: ISC: ISC is a different licence from MIT.
- Remix Icon: Its own licence, Remix Icon License v1.0: It is not MIT. The repository and the npm package name different licences, so the set is unclear.
- Material Symbols and Material Design Icons: Apache-2.0: Apache-2.0 is not MIT.
- Font Awesome Free: Icons CC BY 4.0, fonts OFL 1.1, code MIT: The icons are under a Creative Commons licence and the fonts under OFL.
- Simple Icons: CC0-1.0: CC0 is not MIT.
- Octicons: MIT, with an exception: The licence file is MIT, but the README says the GitHub logos follow GitHub's logo guidelines. The set holds files that are not under MIT.

### What not to change

Everything above is safe to change. These are not, and each has a reason.

- **The colour scales.** Components read semantic tokens. Change those, in [a theme of your own](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/themes/), not the palette they are built on.
- **The status colours.** `--luz-color-success`, `--luz-color-warning`, `--luz-color-danger` and `--luz-color-info` mean what their names say. Do not use them for anything else.
- **The focus ring.** You can set its colour. You cannot remove it.
- **The 44px targets.** The control heights, `--luz-control-sm` to `--luz-control-xl`, are not knobs.
- **The files in `dist/`.** They are generated and replaced on every release. Your changes belong in your own CSS.

## With a bundler or framework
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/bundler/

Import LUZ's CSS and script in Astro or any tool that resolves package names, and keep the layer order and the fonts.

### The imports

Import the CSS of each package you use, tokens first, and the script if you want behaviour. A bundler resolves these names from `node_modules`; a `<link>` in HTML cannot.

The imports
```js
import "@luz-ds/tokens/css";
import "@luz-ds/core/css";
import "@luz-ds/core";

// Only if the page uses a site element: search, consent, language switch
import "@luz-ds/site/css";
import "@luz-ds/site";

// Only for one kind of site: landing, cms or app
import "@luz-ds/landing/css";
```

- The tokens come first: every other package needs them.
- `import "@luz-ds/core"` is the script. It is optional: every LUZ page works without it.
- To load less CSS, import `@luz-ds/core/base.css` and then one file per component, for example `@luz-ds/core/components/button.css`.
- To load one script module, import it by name and call its function: see [JavaScript modules](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/javascript/).

For the lines that match what you are building, with the CDN tags and their integrity hashes, [choose your snippet](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/snippet/).

Every name above is an entry of the `exports` map of its package. This table lists all of them.

The exports of each package

- `@luz-ds/tokens`: `.`: `luz-tokens.css`, the same file as `./css`, for tools that look for the main stylesheet of a package
- `@luz-ds/tokens`: `./css`: `luz-tokens.css`: every token, with the `@font-face` rules of ET Book
- `@luz-ds/tokens`: `./css/min`: `luz-tokens.min.css`: the same, minified
- `@luz-ds/tokens`: `./tokens.css`: `tokens.css`: every token, with no `@font-face`. For when you bring your own font
- `@luz-ds/tokens`: `./fonts.css`: The `@font-face` rules alone
- `@luz-ds/tokens`: `./tokens.json`: The tokens as JSON, for tooling
- `@luz-ds/tokens`: `./dtcg`: The tokens in the W3C Design Tokens format, for Figma and other design tools
- `@luz-ds/tokens`: `./dtcg/resolver`: A resolver document for the same tokens, with their three color modes
- `@luz-ds/tokens`: `./fonts/*`: The ET Book font files that the stylesheets point to
- `@luz-ds/tokens`: `./classes.json`: Every class and custom property the package defines, with its kind and layer, as JSON for tools and AI agents
- `@luz-ds/core`: `.`: `luz.js`: the script, which starts every behaviour on the page. Import it in the browser
- `@luz-ds/core`: `./css`: `luz.css`: the reset, the bare elements, the layout objects, the components and the utilities
- `@luz-ds/core`: `./css/min`: `luz.min.css`: the same, minified
- `@luz-ds/core`: `./base.css`: The settings, the reset and the bare elements, for loading components one by one
- `@luz-ds/core`: `./print.css`: The print styles alone. `luz.css` already has them
- `@luz-ds/core`: `./classless.css`: Styles for markup you cannot add classes to, inside `data-luz-classless`
- `@luz-ds/core`: `./components/*`: One stylesheet per component, such as `@luz-ds/core/components/button.css`
- `@luz-ds/core`: `./themes/*`: The template of a look of your own, `themes/_template.css`
- `@luz-ds/core`: `./theme`: Color mode: `initThemeSystem`, `applyTheme`
- `@luz-ds/core`: `./sidebar`: Scroll spy and the drawer: `initSidebar`
- `@luz-ds/core`: `./clipboard`: Copy buttons: `initCopyButtons`
- `@luz-ds/core`: `./modal`: The fallback for `command` and `commandfor` on a dialog: `initModals`
- `@luz-ds/core`: `./highlight`: Code highlighting: `initHighlight`
- `@luz-ds/core`: `./player`: Audio and video players: `initPlayers`
- `@luz-ds/core`: `./tabs`: Tabs: `initTabs`
- `@luz-ds/core`: `./midi`: The MIDI player: `MidiPlayer`, loaded on demand
- `@luz-ds/core`: `./table-sort`: Sortable tables: `initTableSort`, loaded on demand
- `@luz-ds/core`: `./timeline`: The `<luz-timeline>` element, loaded on demand
- `@luz-ds/core`: `./utils`: Helpers such as `formatTime` and `enableJs`
- `@luz-ds/core`: `./i18n`: The strings of the scripts: `t`, `registerLocale`, `loadLocales`
- `@luz-ds/core`: `./i18n/*`: The strings of one language LUZ ships, for example `@luz-ds/core/i18n/es`: its default export is an object of strings, loaded on demand
- `@luz-ds/core`: `./classes.json`: Every class and custom property the package defines, with its kind and layer, as JSON for tools and AI agents
- `@luz-ds/core`: `./custom-elements.json`: Every custom element the package defines or styles, with its attributes and events, in the Custom Elements Manifest format, for editors and AI agents
- `@luz-ds/site`: `.`: `site.js`: loads the script of each site element the page has
- `@luz-ds/site`: `./search`: The `<luz-search>` element
- `@luz-ds/site`: `./consent`: The `<luz-consent>` element, and `getConsent`
- `@luz-ds/site`: `./mode`: The `<luz-mode>` element
- `@luz-ds/site`: `./css`: `site.css`: the styles of the site elements
- `@luz-ds/site`: `./css/min`: `site.min.css`: the same, minified
- `@luz-ds/site`: `./print.css`: The print rules of the site elements, alone
- `@luz-ds/site`: `./components/*`: One stylesheet per site element: banner, consent, language switch, mode, search and submenu
- `@luz-ds/site`: `./classes.json`: Every class and custom property the package defines, with its kind and layer, as JSON for tools and AI agents
- `@luz-ds/site`: `./custom-elements.json`: Every custom element the package defines or styles, with its attributes and events, in the Custom Elements Manifest format, for editors and AI agents
- `@luz-ds/landing`: `./css`: `landing.css`: the pieces of a landing page
- `@luz-ds/landing`: `./css/min`: `landing.min.css`: the same, minified
- `@luz-ds/landing`: `./components/*`: One stylesheet per piece
- `@luz-ds/landing`: `./classes.json`: Every class and custom property the package defines, with its kind and layer, as JSON for tools and AI agents
- `@luz-ds/cms`: `./css`: `cms.css`: the pieces of a blog or CMS
- `@luz-ds/cms`: `./css/min`: `cms.min.css`: the same, minified
- `@luz-ds/cms`: `./components/*`: One stylesheet per piece
- `@luz-ds/cms`: `./classes.json`: Every class and custom property the package defines, with its kind and layer, as JSON for tools and AI agents
- `@luz-ds/app`: `./css`: `app.css`: the pieces of a web application
- `@luz-ds/app`: `./css/min`: `app.min.css`: the same, minified
- `@luz-ds/app`: `./components/*`: One stylesheet per piece
- `@luz-ds/app`: `./classes.json`: Every class and custom property the package defines, with its kind and layer, as JSON for tools and AI agents

### The layer order survives bundling

Every CSS file LUZ publishes starts with the same `@layer` statement, which declares the order of all of LUZ's layers. So the order is the same however your tool splits, reorders or joins the files: the first one to load sets it.

In the Astro build below, the layers came out in the declared order, `luz.tokens` first and `luz.print` last, and an unlayered rule of the consumer came last.

CSS of your own that is outside any layer wins over every layer of LUZ, in any position, with no `!important`. [Cascade layers](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/layers/) has the full list and how to override one.

### Astro, step by step

A new Astro project with LUZ's tokens and core, a layout that loads them, and CSS of your own that comes last.

**Built with Astro 7.3 on 2026-10-15.** LUZ is in beta and Astro changes between releases, so this page is dated: if a step fails on a newer Astro, check that release's notes first.

The build used packages packed from the LUZ repository at version 0.0.0, installed with `npm install --legacy-peer-deps`, because the peer ranges of `^0.1.0` do not resolve until 0.1.0 is published. After that, the command below needs no flag.

#### The project

The files of the project
```text
my-site/
├─ package.json
├─ astro.config.mjs            (empty config: defineConfig({}))
└─ src/
   ├─ layouts/Base.astro       the two CSS imports, the script
   ├─ styles/site.css          your own CSS, last, outside any layer
   └─ pages/index.astro
```

`astro.config.mjs` stays as Astro creates it. LUZ needed no setting in it.

#### The commands

The commands
```bash
npm create astro@latest my-site
cd my-site
npm install @luz-ds/tokens @luz-ds/core
npm run dev
```

#### The layout

src/layouts/Base.astro
```html
---
// src/layouts/Base.astro
import "@luz-ds/tokens/css";
import "@luz-ds/core/css";
import "../styles/site.css";
---
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
    <title>My site</title>
  </head>
  <body>
    <slot />
    <script>
      import "@luz-ds/core";
    </script>
  </body>
</html>
```

#### Your CSS and the page

src/styles/site.css
```css
/* src/styles/site.css */
:root { --luz-type-base: 1.125rem; }
```

src/pages/index.astro
```html
---
// src/pages/index.astro
import Base from "../layouts/Base.astro";
---
<Base>
  <main class="o-container">
    <h1>My site</h1>
    <button class="luz-btn luz-btn--primary" type="button">Save changes</button>
  </main>
</Base>
```

The rule in `site.css` sets the type knob to 1.125rem and wins over LUZ's default without a layer and without `!important`. [Make it yours](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/make-it-yours/) has the other knobs.

#### What the build showed

- `astro build` and `astro dev` both worked with the two CSS imports in the frontmatter of a layout and no setting in `astro.config.mjs`.
- Astro bundled the `<script>` with `import "@luz-ds/core"` into one module file and split the lazy chunks off it.
- The fonts came out as hashed files, and the layers and your own rule came out in the order described above.

The build output was inspected, and the built page was not opened in a browser. Astro with a view transition router (`<ClientRouter />`) was not tried, and neither was Windows. The `landing`, `cms` and `app` imports have the same shape as the ones above, and were not built.

### Vite, Next, Nuxt and SvelteKit

Only Astro was built for this page; Vite on its own, Next, Nuxt and SvelteKit were not built or tested. The imports are the same ones, in the root layout or the entry file of the app. Each tool's own documentation says where CSS from a package goes:

- [Vite documentation](https://vite.dev/guide/)
- [Next.js documentation](https://nextjs.org/docs)
- [Nuxt documentation](https://nuxt.com/docs)
- [SvelteKit documentation](https://svelte.dev/docs/kit)

One fact is the same for all of them. A LUZ module has no side effect when it is imported, until you call its `init` function, and `luz.js` and `site.js` check that `document` exists first. So a framework that renders on the server can import them. In plain Node, with no `document`, ten modules of core and site were imported with no error.

### Fonts and assets

`@luz-ds/tokens/css` is `luz-tokens.css`, and its `@font-face` rules point at the ET Book files with `url()`. Your bundler resolves those paths: Astro emitted the files as hashed `woff2` assets.

To skip ET Book, import `@luz-ds/tokens/tokens.css` instead. It has the same tokens and no `@font-face`, so no font is downloaded. Then set `--luz-font-body` to the font you use: [Make it yours](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/make-it-yours/) shows how.

### A CDN in a framework

You can load LUZ from a CDN in a framework layout instead of importing it. In an Astro layout, a `<link rel="stylesheet">` in the `<head>` and a `<script type="module" src="https://…">`, each with `integrity` and `crossorigin`, stay as written. So does a script with `is:inline`. Astro only processes a `<script>` that has no attribute other than `src`.

Use the CDN or the imports, not both: LUZ would load twice. [Choose your snippet](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/snippet/) gives the tags with their hashes.

### If something does not work

- **A warning about a peer dependency.** `@luz-ds/core` asks for `@luz-ds/tokens` at `^0.1.0`. Install both, at the same version: `npm install @luz-ds/tokens @luz-ds/core`.
- **The tool cannot resolve `@luz-ds/core/css`.** The export is `./css`, with no file extension. If your tool reports an unresolved import, add the package to `vite.ssr.noExternal`, as [Astro's styling guide](https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/styling/) describes.
- **The styles come out in the wrong order.** Two copies of LUZ on the page, for example one from a CDN and one from your bundler, put their rules in the same layers: load it once. An `@import` with `layer(luz)` nests the names as `luz.luz.components`: drop the `layer()`. [Cascade layers](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/layers/) explains the order.

astro.config.mjs with the package left to the bundler
```js
// astro.config.mjs
import { defineConfig } from "astro/config";

export default defineConfig({
  vite: { ssr: { noExternal: ["@luz-ds/tokens", "@luz-ds/core"] } },
});
```

## JavaScript modules
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/javascript/

What each optional script adds, how to load only the one you need, and what a page does without them.

Every LUZ page works without JavaScript. The scripts add behaviour on top: copying, highlighting, a cycling color mode button, scroll spy, players, tabs, sorting a table and a timeline.

### Load all of it, or one module

All modules markup
```html
<script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/core@0.1.0/dist/luz.min.js"></script>
```

One module code
```js
import { initTabs } from "@luz-ds/core/tabs";
initTabs();
```

- `luz.js` starts every module when the page loads.
- Importing a single module does nothing until you call its `init` function.
- `midi.js`, `table-sort.js` and `timeline.js` are chunks of their own: `luz.js` loads each one on demand, and only on a page that needs it.
- The site search is in `@luz-ds/site`: see [Search](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/site/search/). So is the cookie banner, a module of its own that `site.js` does not include: see [Cookie consent](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/site/consent/). The Auto color mode is a third module of the same kind, `mode.js`, loaded by `site.js` only on a page with a `<luz-mode>`: see [Auto color mode](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/site/mode/).

### The modules

**All 13 JavaScript modules**

#### Languages and the strings scripts write

English is in the entry. Every other language LUZ ships is a small file, fetched at start for a page whose `<html lang>`, or any `lang` outside a link or an option, names it; a page in English makes no request. With the individual modules, call `loadLocales()` yourself, and `await loadLocales()` before `initHighlight()`, `initPlayers()` and `initThemeCycle()`. A file that cannot load is one console warning, and English.

For a language LUZ does not ship, set `data-luz-label-*` once on `<html>` or `<body>`, or call `registerLocale()` before the scripts start.

To check the file, put an import map with an `integrity` section for it before the first module script, on the pages in that language only. A `modulepreload` link with `integrity` is not a guard in Safari or Firefox: use it as a performance hint.

A language for LUZ is a pull request: the JSON file `packages/core/src/i18n/<code>.json`, one line in the `files` map of `i18n.js` and a budget row. The steps are in AGENTS.md.

### Without JavaScript

What each behaviour falls back to when the script does not run:

- [Tabs](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/tabs/): Links, and every panel stacked
- [Color mode switcher](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/mode-switcher/): Three radios that still change the mode; not remembered
- [Auto color mode](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/site/mode/): The four radios still change the mode; Auto is light, and neither the system nor the clock is followed
- [Copy button](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/copy-button/): Hidden; the text stays selectable
- [Player](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/player/): The browser's own media controls; MIDI shows its fallback text
- [Modal](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/modal/): Opens where the browser supports `command`; elsewhere the open button does nothing
- [Code](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/code/): Plain text, no colours
- [Table](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/table/): A heading with a link sorts on the server; a plain heading is not sortable. Rows are never hidden
- [Timeline](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/timeline/): An ordered list with a line and a dot per item; every item is visible
- [Sidebar](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/sidebar/): Works, drawer included; the current link does not follow the scroll
- [Table of contents](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/cms/toc/) and other `data-luz-spy` lists: Links to the sections; no link is marked as the one in view

## Cascade layers
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/layers/

How LUZ sits in your cascade: one layer called luz, the order to declare, and how to override it with no !important.

### Declare the order first

All of LUZ's CSS is inside one cascade layer, `luz`. Put it between your reset and your own styles, and declare that order before any stylesheet loads.

Layer order
```css
@layer reset, luz, app;
```

- The order of layers is the order in which their names first appear. A statement like this one, before everything else, fixes it.
- In HTML, put it in a `<style>` before the `<link>` elements. In a stylesheet, make it the first line, before any `@import` of LUZ.
- A later layer wins over an earlier one. So `app` wins over `luz`, and `luz` over `reset`.
- You do not have to use these names. Use whatever layers you have: `luz` is the only name LUZ adds.

Layers, and names with a dot such as `luz.components`, work in every current browser and have been available since March 2022 ([MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@layer)).

### What is inside luz

Core and the other packages put their rules in their own layers inside `luz`. They are listed here from first to last: a layer lower in the table wins over the ones above it.

- `luz.tokens`: tokens: The `--luz-*` custom properties
- `luz.themes`: core: Your own looks (only custom properties; [make one](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/themes/)). LUZ ships none: its default look is in `luz.tokens`
- `luz.settings`: core: Motion, z-index and breakpoint settings
- `luz.generic`: core: The reset
- `luz.elements`: core: Bare HTML elements, at specificity 0
- `luz.objects`: core: Layout objects: `.o-*`
- `luz.components`: core: The components: `.luz-*`
- `luz.utilities`: core: Single-purpose helpers: `.u-*`. They win over components by order, not by `!important`
- `luz.site`: site: The five site components: `<luz-search>`, `<luz-consent>`, `<luz-lang-switch>`, `<luz-submenu>`, `<luz-banner>` and their `.luz-<tag>__*` classes
- `luz.landing`: landing: The patterns of a landing page: `.luz-landing-*`. After site, so they can build on it
- `luz.cms`: cms: The patterns of a blog, a newspaper or any CMS: `.luz-cms-*`. After site; landing and cms share no class, so their order decides nothing
- `luz.app`: app: The header and the dashboard of a web application: `.luz-app-*`. After cms; landing, cms and app share no class, so their order decides nothing
- `luz.print`: core: What changes on paper, inside `@media print`: [Print styles](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/print/). Last, so it wins over the screen styles of every package

Every file LUZ publishes repeats the order of this list first, so it is the same whichever file a page loads first. These names are public: renaming one is a breaking change.

### CSS without a layer wins

Styles that are not in any layer win over every layer, whatever the order in the source. So a plain rule of yours beats `luz`, and it also beats your own `app` layer.

- If your CSS is not in layers at all, nothing changes for you: it already wins over LUZ, with no `!important`.
- If you use layers, keep your rules in one: a plain rule that you forgot to put in a layer will override your own layers.
- A plain rule is the one place a layer order does not help. Put an override in `app` or in no layer at all, and know which one you chose.

### Override LUZ

Three overrides, from the smallest. Each wins over LUZ because `app` comes after `luz`.

Overriding LUZ from your own layer
```css
@layer reset, luz, app;

@layer app {
  /* A token: every component that reads it follows */
  :root {
    --luz-brand-fill: #0b5a8c;
  }

  /* A component: your rule, in your layer */
  .luz-btn {
    min-height: 3rem;
  }

  /* A site component */
  luz-banner {
    font-size: 1rem;
  }
}
```

- **Prefer tokens.** A token changes every component that reads it, in the mode it is set for. Check the colors you set with [the contrast check](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/contrast/).
- **No `!important` and no longer selectors** are needed: layer order decides first, and specificity only counts inside one layer.
- Keep a color override in the right mode: `:root` in `app` wins over LUZ's dark mode too. Set the token per mode, for example in `[data-theme="dark"]`.

### Why one container layer

LUZ's layers used to be six top-level names: `settings`, `generic`, `elements`, `objects`, `components` and `utilities`. They are short and common, and other tools use some of the same names. A page that loaded one of them next to LUZ merged its `components` or `utilities` with LUZ's, and the order between them was an accident.

- Inside `luz`, LUZ's layer names cannot meet yours.
- One name orders all of LUZ: you place `luz` once, and you do not have to know what is inside.
- It works from a `<link>` or a CDN, where a layer cannot be added from the outside.

You can still put your own layer between two of LUZ's by naming them in the first statement: `@layer luz.components, mine, luz.utilities;`.

### Loading with @import

With a bundler that resolves package names, or with paths to the files, load them as they are. Do not add `layer(luz)` to the import: the files already declare their layers inside `luz`, and wrapping them would nest the names as `luz.luz.components`.

Importing LUZ
```css
@layer reset, luz, app;

@import url("@luz-ds/tokens/css");
@import url("@luz-ds/core/css");
@import url("@luz-ds/site/css");
@import url("@luz-ds/landing/css"); /* only for a landing page */
@import url("@luz-ds/cms/css");     /* only for a blog or a newspaper */
@import url("@luz-ds/app/css");     /* only for a web application */
```

Your own stylesheet imports a file after the statement, so the order is set before LUZ loads.

## Print styles
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/print/

What LUZ changes on paper, and how to keep or change any of it, with one layer and no extra file when you load luz.css.

### What changes on paper

A page printed from LUZ is black text on white, without the parts that only work on a screen. It is one block of CSS in its own layer, `luz.print`, which loads with `luz.css`.

- **Colors.** Surfaces are white and text is black, whichever color mode the page was in. The tokens are set again for print, so every component follows, with no rule of its own. Status colors and code colors become black: each has an icon, a title or a weight besides its color.
- **Hidden.** Navigation (`nav`), the sidebar, the tab row, copy buttons, the color mode switch, the player, toasts and tooltips. Site also hides its skip link and search.
- **Links.** An external link prints its address after its text, in brackets. A link that looks like a button does not.
- **Breaks.** No page break inside a figure, a code block, a table, a table row, a quotation, an image, a card or an alert. A heading stays with the text after it.
- **Tables.** The header row repeats on every page of a table that spans pages. A wide table is not clipped.
- **Code.** A long line wraps, as paper cannot scroll.
- **Tabs.** Every panel prints, one after the other, not only the open one.
- **Motion.** No transition or animation, and no shadows.

### Loading it

- `luz.css` includes it. Nothing to add, and nothing to remove: the block is inside the file.
- If you load `base.css` and components one by one, print is not there. Add `@luz-ds/core/print.css` (`dist/print.css`) if you want it. It declares the layer order itself, as every file does.
- A site page also gets its own print rules, in `luz.site`.
- On a screen nothing changes: the whole block is inside `@media print`.

### Keep or change something

Your CSS wins over `luz.print`, as it wins over the rest of LUZ: a rule in your `app` layer, or in no layer at all. Put it in `@media print`.

Changing the print styles
```css
@layer reset, luz, app;

@layer app {
  @media print {
    /* Print the breadcrumb of this site */
    .site-breadcrumb {
      display: block;
    }

    /* Keep the page margins your own */
    @page {
      margin: 2cm;
    }
  }
}
```

- LUZ sets no `@page` margin and no paper size: they are yours.
- With `luz.css` there is no switch to turn them off: undo the rules you do not want in your own layer, as above. To have none of them, load `base.css` and the components one by one, and do not load `print.css`.

### What is not covered

- **Emulated, not printed.** The test renders a docs page with print media and reads the styles, in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. No one has looked at a printed sheet, or at a PDF made by any browser.
- **The address of a link is drawn by CSS.** It is on paper and in a PDF's text, but not in the page, so a screen reader does not read it.
- **Backgrounds.** Browsers drop background colors and images when they print unless the reader turns "background graphics" on. LUZ relies on text, borders and weight, not on a filled background, to tell things apart.
- **Long tables and breaks.** A table taller than a page breaks anyway: the browser ignores "no break" when it cannot keep it. Safari does not honor `break-after: avoid`, so a heading may be left alone at the foot of a page there.

## Working with AI
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/ai/

What an AI coding agent can read, how to check what it wrote, and the accessibility reviewer you can give it.

### Check what an agent wrote

`npx @luz-ds/check` reads the HTML and CSS of a project, offline, and says which LUZ classes, elements, load order and color tokens are wrong. It reads files and writes nothing. It needs Node 20 or later.

The files an agent can read are linked from `llms.txt`. The commands with paths, the options and exit codes (`npx @luz-ds/check --help`), a sample of the output, the fields of `--json` and the tables of the files and of the rules are on the page at the URL above.

### What check blocks and what it warns about

Each rule has an id such as `class/unknown`, shown in every finding. A rule that blocks makes the exit code 1. A rule that warns does not, unless you pass `--strict`. The two tables are written from the list of rules the command has.

### The accessibility reviewer

The same package prints an agent definition for an AI coding assistant: a reviewer that reads the source of a page and gives advice on accessibility. Copy it into your project.

The command that copies the reviewer
```bash
npx @luz-ds/check agent > .claude/agents/luz-accessibility-reviewer.md
```

- **It overwrites.** The `>` replaces a file that is already there. Use another path, or put your copy under version control first, if you edited it.
- **It is read-only.** It has three tools, `Read`, `Grep` and `Glob`: it reads, searches and lists files, and writes nothing. Read-only does not mean harmless, because `Read` has no path limit. Read the file before you use it, and review any change to it as you would code.

The other notes on the reviewer are on the page at the URL above.

### What this does not do

A run with no findings says what the checker did not find in the files it read. It is not a test of the page.

- **It does not run a browser.** It reads files, so anything that depends on how a page renders, such as layout, focus order or the colors a browser works out, is not seen.
- **Contrast is measured for your tokens only.** It measures the `--luz-*` colors you set in your own color tokens file. A color written straight into a rule is not measured against anything. How the pairs are read is on [Contrast check](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/contrast/).
- **A class built at run time is not seen.** A name put together in a script, such as `"luz-" + name`, or written by a template, is not in the file, so it is not checked.
- **It does not check names, labels, alt text, headings and language.** Whether a button has a name, an image a useful alternative, the headings an order and the page a language is not read, and a run with no findings says nothing about them.
- **It does not replace testing with a screen reader.** No assistive technology is used, by the command or by the reviewer. What has not been tested is listed in [the accessibility statement](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/accessibility/#h-a11y-not-tested).
- **It does not call a network.** It runs offline, with the data in your `node_modules` or in its own package.
- **Discovery by `llms.txt` is by link.** This site is not at the root of a host, so an agent does not find the file by itself: give it the URL, as the prompt above does.
- **Exit code 0 is not an accessibility result.** It says that no rule above blocks in the files that were read.
- **The messages are in English.** They are not translated, whatever the language of the page.

## Classless styles
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/classless/
Files: classless.css

The look of a button, a text field, a select and a table, and the space between paragraphs, headings and lists, on the bare element, inside one element you mark, for markup you cannot add classes to.

### What it is

One extra file, `classless.css`, that gives a bare `button`, `input`, `textarea`, `select` and `table` the look of the LUZ component, and the blocks of long text the space between them, inside an element that has `data-luz-classless`. It is for markup you do not control: a Markdown file, a CMS, a form from a library.

It is not in `luz.css`, and it does nothing until you load it and mark a zone. A page that does not load it is exactly what it was.

### Loading it

From a CDN, with a `<link>` for each file, in this order:

Loading classless.css from a CDN
```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/tokens@0.1.0/dist/luz-tokens.min.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/core@0.1.0/dist/luz.min.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@luz-ds/core@0.1.0/dist/classless.min.css">
```

With a bundler, import the packages' CSS entry points. A `href` cannot name a package: these paths are for `import` only.

Importing classless.css
```js
import "@luz-ds/tokens/css";
import "@luz-ds/core/css";
import "@luz-ds/core/classless.css";
```

Then mark the zone:

Marking the zone
```html
<!-- the whole page -->
<body data-luz-classless>

<!-- or only the rendered content -->
<article data-luz-classless>…</article>
```

- It declares the layer order itself, as every file does, and writes in `luz.elements`. A `.luz-*` class is in `luz.components` and wins by order.
- Put the attribute on `<body>` or an element inside it. The elements it styles are its *descendants*.
- Size: about 1.7 kB min+gzip, with a budget of its own (3 kB).

### What each element becomes

Bare element, and the component it copies

- `button`, `input` of type `button`, `reset`: `.luz-btn .luz-btn--secondary`: Sizes and the other variants: add the class
- `button type="submit"`, `input type="submit"`: `.luz-btn .luz-btn--primary`: A button with no `type` is a submit button to the browser, but not here: say `type="submit"`
- `input` of type text, email, password, search, tel, url, number, date, time, datetime-local, month, week; `textarea`: `.luz-input`, `.luz-input--textarea`: The label, helper and error of `.luz-field`
- `select`: The closed box of `.luz-select`: The styled open list, where the browser has `appearance: base-select`: that is `.luz-select`
- `table`, with its caption, `th` and `td`: `.luz-table`: Scrolling and stacking: they need a wrapper and `data-label`

Not styled, on purpose: `checkbox`, `radio`, `range`, `color`, `file` and `hidden` inputs have a native control of their own, and a `table` is never given `display: block` or a scroll box, which makes some screen readers lose its table semantics.

### Space between blocks

LUZ's reset removes every margin, so a Markdown article would run together. Inside the zone, a paragraph, list, quotation, figure, preformatted block, table, rule, `details`, `fieldset`, `form` or address starts one step (`--luz-space-md`) below the block before it. A heading starts further down (`--luz-space-xl`), and the block that follows it sits closer (`--luz-space-sm`), so each heading belongs to what it introduces.

- The first child of its parent has no margin above it, so the zone does not push itself away from its container.
- `div`, `span` and inline elements are left alone: their layout is yours. For a column of blocks you build yourself, use [`.o-stack`](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/layout/).
- A button that follows a field gets the same step, so it does not touch it. Buttons side by side stay together.
- It is a margin at specificity zero: any class of yours wins, and a LUZ component that sets its own margin keeps it.
- For an article, core's [`.luz-prose`](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/prose/) takes the same three steps between the blocks of one wrapper and adds the line length and the indent of lists. The two work together: put both on the element that holds the text, and classless mode adds the look of its tables and controls.

### How it stays out of the way

- **Specificity zero.** Every selector is inside `:where()`, so any class of yours, in any layer, wins.
- **A LUZ class is left alone.** An element whose class contains `luz-` belongs to its component: a `.luz-copy-btn` inside the zone keeps its own look.
- **A copy, kept honest.** The declarations of the button, field, select and table are those of the components. A test compares each bare element with its component, property by property, and fails when one drifts. The space between blocks is not a copy: no component has it.
- **Everything else about it is the same:** the three color modes, focus ring, right-to-left text and forced colors work as in the component.

### Limits

- **A color mode on the same element.** The date picker and the select take their color scheme from a `data-theme` on an ancestor of the zone, as the components do: set `data-theme` on `<html>`, not on the zone.
- **Checked by script, not by hand.** The parity test passes in Chromium, Firefox 155 and WebKit 26.6, on Linux. Forced colors do not exist in Safari, so that case is checked in Chromium and Firefox only.
- **Not a component.** It has no page in the components gallery and no states of its own. If you can add a class, use the component: it has the variants, sizes and documentation.

## How LUZ is built
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/how-luz-is-built/

Three promises behind every release: it is made for people first and readable by AI agents, every change starts with a failing test, and nothing runs in your page that you did not load.

### Human-first, AI-ready

LUZ is made for the person who uses the page. It starts from native HTML, works with a keyboard and with JavaScript off, and aims for WCAG 2.2 level AA in three color modes.

Plain HTML and CSS with a closed list of class names is also easy for an AI agent to get right. The site publishes the list of names, and a command checks what the agent wrote. [Working with AI](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/ai/) has the files and the prompt.

### Tests first

Every change starts with a failing test. The first commit is a `test:` commit that fails without the change, and the change that follows makes it pass. A bug fix starts with the test that reproduces it.

One command, `pnpm check:all`, runs every check. The rules those checks enforce are in [PRINCIPLES.md](https://github.com/nandovejer/luz/blob/main/PRINCIPLES.md), and [TESTING.md](https://github.com/nandovejer/luz/blob/main/dev/TESTING.md) says how to write the test.

### Zero dependencies

The packages have no runtime dependency. They ship plain CSS and small ES modules that need no build step, and they use the browser's own elements and APIs before any script.

Size budgets are a red line: a check fails when a file grows past its ceiling, and nobody raises a ceiling to make it pass. Everything LUZ ships is under the MIT licence, and only the MIT licence. [Get started](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/) shows how to load it.

## Tokens
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/tokens/

CSS custom properties for every colour, space, size and type value. Use the semantic ones: they change with the color mode.

Level 1 · @luz-ds/tokens

CSS custom properties for every colour, space, size and type value. Use the semantic ones: they change with the color mode.

### Two layers

- **Primitives** hold raw values: `--luz-blue-60`, `--luz-space-md`. They are the same in every mode.
- **Semantic tokens** give a colour a job: `--luz-text-primary`, `--luz-surface-page`. Each mode points them at different primitives.
- Space, size, radius, shadow and type scales are primitives that components use directly: they do not change with the mode.

Where the tokens come from
```text
packages/tokens/tokens.json        the source of the primitives
packages/tokens/src/semantic.css   the semantic colours, per mode
dist/luz-tokens.css                both layers, and the ET Book font
dist/tokens.css                    both layers, no font
```

### Use semantic colours, never primitive ones

A component that uses a primitive colour looks right in one mode and wrong in the others.

Semantic and primitive colour tokens
```css
/* Do: semantic tokens follow the mode */
.panel {
  color: var(--luz-text-primary);
  background: var(--luz-surface);
  border: 1px solid var(--luz-divider);
  padding: var(--luz-space-md);
}

/* Don't: a primitive colour stays the same in dark mode */
.panel {
  color: var(--luz-gray-100);
  background: var(--luz-blue-10);
}
```

### Text on a solid fill

Behind `--luz-text-on-fill`, use a fill token, not the brand or status colour.

- The fills: `--luz-brand-fill`, `--luz-brand-fill-hover`, `--luz-brand-fill-active` and `--luz-color-danger-fill`.
