### Keyboard and ARIA
The native keys apply. Tab moves between controls.

- Space checks a checkbox or a switch.
- Arrow keys choose within a radio group, and move a range slider.
- Group related controls in a `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>`, or a `role="group"` named with `aria-labelledby`.
- Write "Error: " before the error text, hidden visually with `.u-sr-only` if you like.

### When to use
Use these fields to collect input, with the native control that fits the data.

- Text, email, number, date, time: an input of that `type`.
- One choice from a few (six or fewer): radios. From many: a [select](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/select/).
- Several choices: checkboxes. A setting that applies at once: a switch.

### When not to use
Do not rebuild a native control from `<div>` elements.

- Do not use a placeholder as the label: it disappears when the reader types.
- Do not use a switch inside a form that is sent with a button: use a checkbox.
- To show how far a task has got, use [progress](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/progress/), not a [meter](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/meter/).

### Do and don't
- **Do** A checkbox in a form that is sent with a button: nothing changes until “Save preferences”.
- **Don't** A switch in the same form: a switch promises an instant change, so the reader does not know the button is still needed.

### Writing the content
Every control has a visible label that names what to enter.

- Labels are short nouns, in sentence case: "Project name".
- A hint, under the control, says the format or why you ask.
- An error says what is wrong and how to fix it: "Use letters, numbers and dashes only."
- If you mark required fields with "*", say once, above the form, what it means.

## Icon grid
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/icon-grid/
Example: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/examples/components/icon-grid.html
Files: components/icon-grid.css · Package: @luz-ds/core

Lets readers browse a set of icons by name and copy the SVG of each one.

### Known issues
None known.

### Copy the markup
Icon grid markup
```html
<ul class="luz-icon-grid">
  <li class="luz-icon-item">
    <span class="luz-icon-display"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="24" height="24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M12 5v14M5 12h14"/></svg></span>
    <span class="luz-icon-name" id="icon-plus">Plus</span>
    <button class="luz-copy-btn" type="button" id="icon-plus-copy" aria-labelledby="icon-plus-copy icon-plus" data-copy="&lt;svg …&gt;…&lt;/svg&gt;">Copy SVG</button>
  </li>
</ul>
```

The same icons as a sprite: paste it once in the page, then draw each one with `<use>`. The sprite works only in the same document (`href="#id"`); a `<use>` that points at a file on another origin, a CDN included, is blocked by browsers.

Icon sprite markup
```html
<svg width="0" height="0" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false">
  <symbol id="luz-icon-menu" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M4 6h16M4 12h16M4 18h16"/></symbol>
  <symbol id="luz-icon-close" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M6 6l12 12M18 6L6 18"/></symbol>
  <symbol id="luz-icon-search" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><circle cx="11" cy="11" r="6.5"/><path d="M16 16l4.5 4.5"/></symbol>
  <symbol id="luz-icon-check" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M5 12.5l4.5 4.5L19 7"/></symbol>
  <symbol id="luz-icon-plus" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M12 5v14M5 12h14"/></symbol>
  <symbol id="luz-icon-minus" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M5 12h14"/></symbol>
  <symbol id="luz-icon-chevron-down" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M6 9l6 6 6-6"/></symbol>
  <symbol id="luz-icon-chevron-up" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M6 15l6-6 6 6"/></symbol>
  <symbol id="luz-icon-chevron-end" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M9 6l6 6-6 6"/></symbol>
  <symbol id="luz-icon-arrow-end" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M5 12h14M13 6l6 6-6 6"/></symbol>
  <symbol id="luz-icon-cart" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M3 4h2.5l2.2 10.5h9.6L19.5 7H6.2"/><circle cx="9" cy="19" r="1.4"/><circle cx="17" cy="19" r="1.4"/></symbol>
  <symbol id="luz-icon-user" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><circle cx="12" cy="8" r="4"/><path d="M4.5 20.5c.6-4 3.6-6 7.5-6s6.9 2 7.5 6"/></symbol>
  <symbol id="luz-icon-mail" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><rect x="3" y="5" width="18" height="14" rx="2"/><path d="M3.5 7.5l8.5 6 8.5-6"/></symbol>
  <symbol id="luz-icon-calendar" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><rect x="4" y="5" width="16" height="15" rx="2"/><path d="M4 10h16M8.5 3v4M15.5 3v4"/></symbol>
  <symbol id="luz-icon-clock" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8.5"/><path d="M12 7.5V12l3 2"/></symbol>
  <symbol id="luz-icon-map-pin" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M12 21s7-5.8 7-11.5a7 7 0 0 0-14 0C5 15.2 12 21 12 21z"/><circle cx="12" cy="9.5" r="2.5"/></symbol>
  <symbol id="luz-icon-download" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M12 4v11M7.5 11L12 15.5 16.5 11M5 20h14"/></symbol>
  <symbol id="luz-icon-external" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M14 4h6v6M20 4l-9 9M18 14v4.5a1.5 1.5 0 0 1-1.5 1.5h-11A1.5 1.5 0 0 1 4 18.5v-11A1.5 1.5 0 0 1 5.5 6H10"/></symbol>
  <symbol id="luz-icon-info" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8.5"/><path d="M12 11v5.5M12 7.5v.01"/></symbol>
  <symbol id="luz-icon-warning" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M12 4l9 16H3z"/><path d="M12 10v4.5M12 17.5v.01"/></symbol>
  <symbol id="luz-icon-heart" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M12 20s-7.5-4.6-7.5-10.2A4.3 4.3 0 0 1 12 7.2a4.3 4.3 0 0 1 7.5 2.6C19.5 15.4 12 20 12 20z"/></symbol>
  <symbol id="luz-icon-filter" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M4 5h16l-6 7.5V19l-4-2v-4.5z"/></symbol>
</svg>

<svg width="24" height="24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><use href="#luz-icon-cart"/></svg>
```

An icon beside a label, and an icon alone. A button names itself from its text, so give an icon-only button a name in a `.u-sr-only` span, not an `aria-label`: the span is translated with the page.

Icon in a button markup
```html
<!-- With a label: the icon is 16 px inside a button -->
<button class="luz-btn luz-btn--primary" type="submit">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="24" height="24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M3 4h2.5l2.2 10.5h9.6L19.5 7H6.2"/><circle cx="9" cy="19" r="1.4"/><circle cx="17" cy="19" r="1.4"/></svg>
  Add to cart
</button>

<!-- Icon only: the name is real text, hidden from the eye -->
<button class="luz-btn luz-btn--ghost" type="button">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="24" height="24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M4 6h16M4 12h16M4 18h16"/></svg>
  <span class="u-sr-only">Menu</span>
</button>
```

Two icons point to the end of the line: `chevron-end` and `arrow-end`, marked with `data-luz-flip`. In right-to-left text, LUZ mirrors anything with that attribute using the rule below, in core's utilities layer, so you write nothing. Add the attribute to an icon of your own that points to the end of the line.

Right-to-left rule, shipped in luz.utilities
```css
:where([data-luz-flip]):dir(rtl) {
  transform: scaleX(-1);
}
```

### Variants and options
There are no modifiers. The grid fits as many columns of at least 100 px as the width allows.

- `.luz-icon-grid`: The list: a grid with no bullets
- `.luz-icon-item`: One bordered cell: icon, name, copy button
- `.luz-icon-display`: A 48 × 48 px box that centres the icon, in the secondary text colour
- `.luz-icon-name`: The name under the icon

### How it works
A `<ul>` of icons, styled by `components/icon-grid.css`. The copy buttons are [copy buttons](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/copy-button/), wired by `clipboard.js`.

- Each button carries the icon's SVG, escaped, in `data-copy`.
- The 22 icons are LUZ's own, drawn for it on a 24 × 24 grid with a 2 px round stroke in `currentColor`. They are not a package and no file is loaded: copy the SVG, or the sprite, into your page.
- An icon is 24 × 24 px as written, and 16 px inside a `.luz-btn`. For an icon that must follow the text size, set `width="1.5em" height="1.5em"`.

### Without JavaScript
The copy buttons are hidden. The grid still shows every icon and its name.

### Keyboard and ARIA
Tab reaches each copy button; Enter or Space copies the SVG.

- Each button is named by its own text and the icon's name, with `aria-labelledby`: "Copy SVG Plus".
- The icons are `aria-hidden="true"` and `focusable="false"`: the name is the text under them, or the `.u-sr-only` text of the button that holds them.
- Info and warning always come with words. A lone glyph says nothing to someone who cannot see its shape or its colour: put the words beside it, or give a stand-alone icon `role="img"` and a name.
- The result of each copy is announced in a polite live region.

### When to use
Use an icon grid to let readers browse a set of icons and copy the one they need.

### When not to use
Do not use it to lay out icons that do something: it is a catalogue, not a toolbar.

- For a row of actions, use buttons with text in an [action group](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/layout/#objects-actions).
- Never use an icon as the only label of an action: give it its name as text, visible or in a `.u-sr-only` span.
- For a logo or an illustration, use an `<img>` or an SVG at its own size.
- For hundreds of icons, bring your own set: LUZ's has 22.

### Do and don't
- **Do** Name each icon by what it shows, in one word.
- **Don't** File names as labels: “ic_add_24” and “ic_ok_24” make the reader decode them, and “ok” is a use, not what the icon shows.

### Writing the content
Name each icon by what it shows, in one word if you can: "Plus", "Check", "Arrow".

- Keep names unique in one grid.
- Draw every icon on the same grid and stroke, with `currentColor`, so it follows the text colour in every mode.
- Pair **Info** and **Warning** with words, in the same place. They are shapes, not status colours: an alert keeps its own.

## Image
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/image/
Example: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/examples/components/image.html
Files: components/image.css · Package: @luz-ds/core

Shows a picture in a frame of fixed shape, on a flat surface while it loads or when it is missing.

### Known issues
If an image fails to load, some browsers add a broken-image icon next to its alt text. In forced-colors mode the surface takes the page's colour, and the frame shows a thin border instead.

### Copy the markup
Image frame markup
```html
<div class="luz-image">
  <picture>
    <source type="image/avif" srcset="dunes-640.avif 640w, dunes-1280.avif 1280w" sizes="(min-width: 768px) 50vw, 100vw">
    <source type="image/webp" srcset="dunes-640.webp 640w, dunes-1280.webp 1280w" sizes="(min-width: 768px) 50vw, 100vw">
    <img src="dunes-1280.jpg" srcset="dunes-640.jpg 640w, dunes-1280.jpg 1280w" sizes="(min-width: 768px) 50vw, 100vw"
      width="1280" height="720" alt="Sand dunes under a low sun" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
  </picture>
</div>
```

### Variants and options
One modifier sets the shape. Without one, the frame is 16:9.

- `.luz-image`: 16:9
- `.luz-image--4x3`: 4:3
- `.luz-image--3x2`: 3:2
- `.luz-image--1x1`: Square
- `.luz-image--21x9`: 21:9, for wide banners
- `.luz-image--9x16`: 9:16, portrait

### How it works
A `<div>` of fixed aspect ratio around a native `<picture>`, styled by `@luz-ds/core`. No JavaScript.

- The image fills the frame and is cropped to it.
- The frame is a flat `--luz-surface-strong` surface: with no image, while an image loads, or when it fails. A failed image's alt text is drawn on it, and transparent PNG and SVG images sit on it too.
- LUZ ships no placeholder picture: the page asks for nothing it did not name.

### Without JavaScript
Nothing changes: the frame and the image are HTML and CSS. Without CSS the image shows at its own size.

### Keyboard and ARIA
The frame has no interaction of its own.

- Screen readers announce the `<img>` by its alt text; an empty frame announces nothing.
- Do not add a role or an `aria-label` to the frame.
- If the image is a link, the link takes its name from the alt text, which must then say where it goes.

### When to use
Use the image frame for a picture in a box of fixed shape, such as a card cover or an article header, when the picture may be missing.

- Content from people or from a content system.
- A page built before its images exist.

### When not to use
Do not use it for an image that must keep its own shape, such as a chart or a screenshot: the frame crops it.

- For a chart or a diagram with a caption, use a [figure](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/figure/).
- For icons and logos, use an `<img>` or an SVG at its own size.
- Never let an empty frame stand in for an image that carries information: if it is missing, say so in text.

### Do and don't
- **Do** A real image, with an alt text that says what it shows.
- **Don't** An empty frame where the content is the image: a floor plan nobody can see, with nothing in words.

### Writing the content
Give every real image an alt text that says what it shows, in one plain sentence.

- Use `alt=""` when the image is decorative, or the text next to it already says the same.
- The frame crops: keep text and essential detail away from the edges, and describe what stays visible.
- Set `width` and `height` to the image's own size, so the page does not jump while it loads.
- Add `loading="lazy"` only below the fold; an image visible when the page opens should load at once.
- Do not put text in images.

## Meta line
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/meta/
Example: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/examples/components/meta.html
Files: components/meta.css · Package: @luz-ds/core

Shows a few facts about something on one line, such as its date, its reading time and its author, with a dot between them.

### Known issues
The dots are hidden from screen readers with alternative text for generated content, which Firefox has since version 128 and Safari since 17.4. An older browser lets a screen reader read each dot. Not yet tested with a screen reader.

### Copy the markup
Meta line markup
```html
<p class="luz-meta">
  <span>By <a href="/authors/ana-ruiz/">Ana Ruiz</a></span>
  <time datetime="2026-10-12">12 October 2026</time>
  <span>6 min read</span>
</p>
```

### Variants and options
There are no modifiers.

- `.luz-meta`: The line: facts in a row that wraps, in the sans, in the secondary text colour
- Each child: One fact: a `<time>`, a link, or a `<span>` of text. Every child after the first gets a dot before it

### How it works
CSS only, in `components/meta.css`: a flex row that wraps, and a dot drawn by `::before` on each fact after the first.

- The dot sits in the gap before its fact. The line clips its start and end edges, so a fact that wraps to the start of a new line leaves its dot outside: no line starts with a dot.
- The line has 4 px of padding at each end, room for a link's focus ring inside the clip, and a negative margin of the same size, so its text lines up with the text above it.
- The dot is written `content: "·" / ""`: an empty alternative text, so screen readers do not read it.
- Nothing in it is positioned, so in a card whose title link covers the card, the whole card stays one link.

### Without JavaScript
Nothing changes: the meta line is CSS. Without CSS, the facts run together on one line with the spaces of your markup between them: keep a space or a line break between the elements.

### Keyboard and ARIA
The line takes no focus and adds no role. Tab reaches the links in it, in order.

- A screen reader reads the facts one after another, without the dots. Write each fact so it makes sense alone: "6 min read", not "6".
- Give a date a `<time datetime>`, so software can read it.

### When to use
Use a meta line for two to four short facts about a post, a story or an item: the author, the date, the reading time, the section.

### When not to use
Do not use it for a sentence, or for facts the reader needs to compare across items.

- Facts with labels, such as a price and a size, are a description list (`<dl>`) or a [table](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/table/).
- A path of pages is a [breadcrumb](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/breadcrumb/); a set of labels is a row of [tags](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/tag/).

### Do and don't
- **Do** Each fact in its own element, and the dots left to CSS.
- **Don't** Dots typed into the text: a screen reader reads each one, and a wrapped line can start with one.

### Writing the content
Short facts, the most useful first: usually the author, then the date.

- Write the date in words, with the month spelled out, in the reader's language.
- Two to four facts. More than that is a list, not a line.

## Meter
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/meter/
Example: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/examples/components/meter.html
Files: components/meter.css · Package: @luz-ds/core

Draws a value in a known range as a bar, next to its figure, with the native meter element.

### Known issues
None known.

### Copy the markup
A bar in the cell of its figure, in a table. The figure is text, so the bar is a picture of it and is hidden from assistive technology:

Meter in a table cell markup
```html
<td class="luz-table__numeric" data-label="Parcels">1,204<meter class="luz-meter" value="1204" min="0" max="1500" aria-hidden="true">1,204 of 1,500</meter></td>
```

A bar on its own, with a visible name and the figure in it:

Meter with a visible label markup
```html
<label for="storage">Storage used, 6 of 10 GB</label>
<meter class="luz-meter" id="storage" value="6" min="0" max="10">6 of 10 GB</meter>
```

### Variants and options
One class. The bar comes from the native attributes.

- `value`, `min` and `max`: The value and its range: `min` is 0 and `max` is 1 if you leave them out. A value outside the range is clamped to it
- `aria-hidden="true"`: For a bar next to its figure: the figure is read, the picture is not
- `low`, `high`, `optimum`: Do not set them: they would only change the colour the browser chooses, and every state is drawn in the brand colour

### How it works
The native `<meter>` element, styled by `components/meter.css`: an 8 px bar, full width of its box and at least 8rem long, with the brand colour as the fill and a 1 px edge in the field border colour, so the whole length shows on any surface.

- The browser draws the fill as `value` between `min` and `max`.
- Every state is the same colour. The figure and the scale say what the value means, not a green or a red: status colours keep their own meanings (alerts, tags).
- Use the same `max` in every row of a table, or the bars lie.
- In forced colors the bar keeps a border and draws the fill in the system highlight colour.
- The text inside the element is the fallback for a browser that does not draw it. Say the figure there too.

### Without JavaScript
The bar shows the value in the markup. Moving it needs your script, which sets `value`.

### Keyboard and ARIA
A meter is not interactive and takes no focus.

- Next to its figure, in the same cell or the same line, hide the bar with `aria-hidden="true"`: the figure is text, and the table is the accessible chart. A reader hears the figure once.
- Put the bar in the cell of its figure, not in a column of its own: a column of bars would read as a column of empty cells. If you do want a column for the bar, each cell carries visible text of its own, such as “80 %”, under a heading that says what it is.
- A meter that is not hidden needs a name: a `<label for>` or `aria-labelledby`. It is then read as “value, minimum, maximum”, so it repeats a figure that is already there: hide it unless it stands alone.
- The bar is a picture of the figure in the same cell: assistive technology reads the figure.

### When to use
Use a meter for a value in a known range, next to its figure, in a few to a few dozen rows that share a scale: a share of a total, a count against a quota.

### When not to use
Do not use a meter for a task that is running: use [progress](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/progress/).

- For a trend over time, use a chart library; keep the [table](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/table/) as its text alternative. LUZ draws no line, area or pie chart.
- When exact values matter more than the shape, leave the bar out: the figure is already there.
- Do not use the bar's colour to say good or bad: it is always the brand colour.

### Do and don't
- **Do** One scale for every row, and the figure beside each bar: the length compares, the number says how much.
- **Don't** A scale of its own in each row: 312 of 400 looks longer than 1,204 of 1,500, and the figure is nowhere to check it.

### Writing the content
The figure is the content; the bar only shows how it compares.

- Put the figure in text in the same cell or line, with its unit in the column heading: “Parcels”.
- Say the scale in the caption or the heading when it is not obvious: “Parcels per route, this week”.
- Inside the element, write the figure and its range as a fallback: “1,204 of 1,500”.

## Modal
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/modal/
Example: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/examples/components/modal.html
Files: components/modal.css · Package: @luz-ds/core

Asks for a decision that must be made before the reader goes on, in a native dialog.

### Known issues
Some supported browsers do not have the `command` and `commandfor` attributes yet. In those browsers, with JavaScript off, the open button does nothing. Give the reader another way to the same action.

### Copy the markup
Modal markup
```html
<button class="luz-btn luz-btn--primary" type="button" commandfor="rename" command="show-modal">Rename project</button>

<dialog class="luz-modal" id="rename" aria-labelledby="rename-title">
  <div class="luz-modal__header">
    <button class="luz-modal__close" type="button" commandfor="rename" command="close" aria-label="Close dialog">×</button>
    <h2 class="luz-modal__title" id="rename-title">Rename project</h2>
  </div>
  <form method="dialog">
    <div class="luz-modal__body">
      <div class="luz-field">
        <label class="luz-field__label" for="rename-name">New name</label>
        <input class="luz-input" id="rename-name" type="text" autofocus>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="luz-modal__footer">
      <button class="luz-btn luz-btn--ghost" type="button" commandfor="rename" command="close">Cancel</button>
      <button class="luz-btn luz-btn--primary" value="rename">Rename project</button>
    </div>
  </form>
</dialog>
```

Fallback script code
```js
import { initModals } from "@luz-ds/core/modal";
initModals();
```

### Variants and options
One size and no modifiers: up to 600 px wide and 90 % of the viewport high, scrolling inside when the content is longer.

- `.luz-modal`: The dialog surface, with a dimmed and slightly blurred backdrop
- `.luz-modal__header`, `__title`: The title row, with a rule under it
- `.luz-modal__close`: The × button, at the end of the title row, 28 px at least
- `.luz-modal__body`: The content
- `.luz-modal__footer`: The buttons, at the end of the row, with a rule above them
- `command="show-modal"`, `command="close"`: Open and close the dialog named in `commandfor`

### How it works
A native `<dialog>`, styled by `components/modal.css` and opened as a modal.

- The browser does the hard part: the page behind is inert, focus stays inside, Escape closes, and focus goes back to the opener.
- Buttons open and close it with `command` and `commandfor`, with no script.
- `initModals()` from `modal.js` handles the same two commands in browsers that do not support them yet, and does nothing in the others. `luz.js` runs it.
- A `<form method="dialog">` inside closes the dialog when it is sent, and its `returnValue` is the value of the button pressed.

### Without JavaScript
In browsers that support `command`, everything works. In the others the open button does nothing: see Known issues.

### Keyboard and ARIA
Tab and Shift+Tab move inside the dialog only; Escape closes it.

- On open, focus goes to the first focusable element, or to the one with `autofocus`.
- Name the dialog with `aria-labelledby` pointing at its title.
- The × button needs `aria-label="Close dialog"`: its text is a symbol.

### When to use
Use a modal to ask for a decision or a short input that must be settled before the reader goes on.

- To confirm an action that cannot be undone.
- To ask for one or two values, such as a new name.

### When not to use
Do not use a modal for something the reader can ignore or come back to.

- For information about the page, use an [alert](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/alert/).
- For a confirmation that needs no answer, use a [toast](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/toast/).
- For a long form, use its own page.
- Never open a modal when the page loads.

### Do and don't
- **Do** The title asks the question and the main button repeats the action.
- **Don't** “Are you sure?” with “Cancel” and “Continue”: the reader has to read the body to know what “Continue” does.

### Writing the content
The title asks the question or names the task: "Delete this draft?"

- The body says what happens, in one or two sentences.
- The main button repeats the action: "Delete draft". The other one is "Cancel".
- Never "OK", "Yes" or "Confirm".

## Navbar
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/navbar/
Example: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/examples/components/navbar.html
Files: components/navbar.css · Package: @luz-ds/core

Puts the main links of a site in a header's row, and in a panel under it on a narrow screen.

### Known issues
If you keep pressing Tab after the last link of the open menu, focus moves on into the page and the menu stays open over it, hiding what is behind. Escape closes it. This meets WCAG 2.4.11 (AA) and does not meet 2.4.12 (AAA).

- **Browsers without anchor positioning.** Where CSS anchor positioning is supported (Chrome and Edge 125, Safari 26, Firefox 147) the panel opens under the bar wherever it ends, even with a notice or the cookie banner above it. Elsewhere it opens at `--luz-bar-h` from the top of the window: with enlarged text and a bar that wraps to a second row, or with a band above the bar before the page scrolls, it can cover part of the bar. Escape or a click outside closes it.
- **Forced colors in Firefox.** The dim layer behind the open menu is not drawn, so the page is not dimmed. The panel keeps its border, so it is still set apart.
- **Breakpoints in Safari on a Mac.** With always-visible scrollbars, Safari does not count the scrollbar in width media queries (WebKit bug 52653), so the menu collapses, or the links return to the row, when the window is up to about 15 px wider than 768 px.

### Copy the markup
The navbar goes in a bar's row, after core's menu button and the site's name. The bar is yours, or the header of a package for one kind of site, which also sets the anchor the panel opens under.

Navbar markup
```html
<header class="o-sticky">
  <div class="o-container o-container--inline o-row">
    <button class="luz-nav-toggle" type="button" popovertarget="site-nav" aria-label="Menu">
      <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="24" height="24" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path fill="currentColor" d="M3 5h18v2H3zM3 11h18v2H3zM3 17h18v2H3z"/></svg>
    </button>
    <a href="/">Acme</a>
    <nav class="luz-navbar" id="site-nav" aria-label="Main" popover>
      <ul class="luz-navbar__list">
        <li><a class="luz-navbar__link" href="/products/" aria-current="page">Products</a></li>
        <li><a class="luz-navbar__link" href="/pricing/">Pricing</a></li>
        <li><a class="luz-navbar__link" href="/support/">Support</a></li>
      </ul>
    </nav>
  </div>
</header>
```

### Variants and options
- `.luz-navbar`: On the `<nav popover>`: a row of the bar from 769 px; a panel under the bar, the width of the window, at 768 px and below
- `.luz-navbar__list`: The `<ul>`: a row that wraps, with no markers; a column in the open panel
- `.luz-navbar__link`: Each link, at least 44 px tall; with `aria-current`, the primary text colour and a 2 px underline
- `anchor-name: --luz-bar`: Set on the bar, with `anchor-scope: --luz-bar`, by the header of a kind of site or by you: the panel opens under it. Without it, the panel opens at `--luz-bar-h` from the top of the window

### How it works
A native `popover` on the `<nav>`, opened by core's `.luz-nav-toggle` with `popovertarget`. No JavaScript: the browser gives Escape, light dismiss, the place of the open panel in the Tab order and the expanded state of the button.

- From 769 px the closed popover is shown as a row of the bar, and the menu button is hidden.
- At 768 px and below the panel is fixed under the bar, the width of the window, with a shadow, and a dim layer that starts under the bar so the bar is never dimmed.
- A panel left open when the window grows stays under the bar until it is closed.
- Without the popover API the links stay in the row and wrap, and the menu button stays hidden.
- The submenu of site ([Submenu](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/site/submenu/)) can go in a list item.

### Without JavaScript
Nothing changes: the navbar is HTML, a native popover and CSS.

### Keyboard and ARIA
Every link is reached with Tab in the order of the page.

- Narrow and closed, the links are not in the Tab order. Enter or Space on the menu button opens the panel, and the next Tab reaches its first link.
- Escape, or a click outside, closes the panel and puts focus back on the button. The button says whether it is expanded.
- Give the `<nav>` a name that no other navigation of the page has, such as "Main".
- Mark the current page with `aria-current="page"`, or `"true"` for the section a page belongs to.

### When to use
Use the navbar for the few main links of a site, in the header every page shares.

### When not to use
Do not use it for an app with many sections, or for links in the page.

- For many sections, or a hierarchy, use the [sidebar](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/sidebar/).
- For the place of a page in a hierarchy, use a [breadcrumb](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/breadcrumb/).
- For the sections of one page, use [tabs](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/tabs/) or a list of in-page links.

### Do and don't
- **Do** A few links with short names, the current one underlined: the row reads in one glance.
- **Don't** Every page of the site in the bar: the row wraps, and nothing stands out as the way in.

### Writing the content
Name each link after the page it opens, in one or two words.

- Five links or fewer; put the rest in the footer, or a [submenu](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/site/submenu/).
- Name the menu button after what it opens: "Menu".

## Pagination
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/pagination/
Example: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/examples/components/pagination.html
Files: components/pagination.css · Package: @luz-ds/core

Links to the pages of a list that goes on over several, with the current page marked.

### Known issues
None known.

### Copy the markup
Pagination markup
```html
<nav aria-label="Pagination">
  <ul class="luz-pagination">
    <li><a class="luz-pagination__link" href="/blog/?page=1" rel="prev">Previous</a></li>
    <li><a class="luz-pagination__link" href="/blog/?page=1" aria-label="Page 1">1</a></li>
    <li><a class="luz-pagination__link" href="/blog/?page=2" aria-label="Page 2" aria-current="page">2</a></li>
    <li><a class="luz-pagination__link" href="/blog/?page=3" aria-label="Page 3">3</a></li>
    <li><a class="luz-pagination__link" href="/blog/?page=3" rel="next">Next</a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>
```

### Variants and options
There are no modifiers. The list wraps onto more lines when it is narrow.

- `.luz-pagination`: The list: one row of items, which wraps when it is narrow
- `.luz-pagination__link`: A page, Previous or Next: a target of at least 44 px
- `aria-current="page"`: Marks the current page: solid fill and heavier weight
- `aria-disabled="true"`: Previous or Next at either end, as a `<span>` and not a link: disabled text colour
- `.luz-pagination__gap`: The “…” of a long list: a mark, hidden from screen readers

### How it works
A `<nav>` landmark around a list of links, styled by `components/pagination.css`. Each page is a real address, so the server renders it and the back button, a bookmark and a search engine all work. No JavaScript.

- The numbers are links, not buttons: following one loads another page.
- `rel="prev"` and `rel="next"` say which links go to the neighbours.
- The current page is a link with `aria-current="page"`, so it is still announced as a link and keeps its place in the order.
- At the first or last page, Previous or Next is a `<span>` with `aria-disabled="true"`: text, with no focus stop.
- Keep the `<nav>`. Some browsers drop the list semantics of a `<ul>` without bullets, and the landmark is what keeps it announced as a list; without a `<nav>`, add `role="list"` to the `<ul>`.

### Without JavaScript
Nothing changes: it is a list of links and CSS. Without CSS it reads as a list of links.

### Keyboard and ARIA
Tab reaches each link in order; Enter follows it.

- Name the `<nav>` “Pagination” with `aria-label`, so it differs from the main navigation.
- Give a number the name “Page 3” with `aria-label`. The visible number stays in the name. `aria-current="page"` makes the screen reader say which one is current, so the name does not need to.
- A gap is `aria-hidden="true"`: the screen reader hears the pages, not the dots.

### When to use
Use pagination when a list is too long for one page and each page can be reached by its own address: search results, a blog archive, a table of records.

### When not to use
Do not use pagination for a short list, or for the steps of a task.

- For the parents of the page you are on, use a [breadcrumb](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/breadcrumb/).
- For the sections of one page, use [tabs](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/tabs/).
- For a feed that keeps loading on scroll, give a link to the next page as well: it is the only version a keyboard and a screen reader reach.

### Do and don't
- **Do** Show the first and last page, the current one and its neighbours, and a gap between.
- **Don't** Print every page of a long list: it grows past the width and the reader has to count.

### Writing the content
Use the word the reader would say.

- “Previous” and “Next”, not arrows alone and not “Back”.
- Page numbers as plain digits; name them “Page 3” for assistive technology.
- Say how many pages there are near the list (“Page 8 of 40”) when the total matters.

## Player
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/player/
Example: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/examples/components/player.html
Files: components/player.css · Package: @luz-ds/core

Plays a video, a sound or a MIDI file in the page, with the same controls for all three.

### Known issues
Captions, transcripts and audio description depend on the media you provide. The colours of the captions are a request: the reader's own caption settings win, and a browser may draw them its own way, in its own full-screen player for example. A MIDI file has no player without JavaScript: offer a download link in the fallback text.

### Copy the markup
An audio player. The video player adds a `.luz-player-media-wrap` around the `<video>` and a mute button and volume slider: copy it from the example above.

Audio player markup
```html
<div class="luz-player" data-type="audio" role="group" aria-label="Episode 12 player">
  <audio class="luz-player-audio" preload="none" controls>
    <source src="episode-12.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
  </audio>
  <div class="luz-player-controls luz-player-controls--audio">
    <button class="luz-player-btn luz-player-playpause" type="button" aria-label="Play">
      <svg class="icon-play" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor" aria-hidden="true"><polygon points="6,3 20,12 6,21"/></svg>
      <svg class="icon-pause" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor" aria-hidden="true" style="display:none"><rect x="5" y="3" width="4" height="18"/><rect x="15" y="3" width="4" height="18"/></svg>
    </button>
    <div class="luz-player-progress-row luz-player-progress-row--audio">
      <span class="luz-player-time luz-player-current">0:00</span>
      <input class="luz-player-seekbar" type="range" min="0" max="1000" step="1" value="0" aria-label="Seek audio">
      <span class="luz-player-time luz-player-duration">0:00</span>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

Captions and subtitles: one `<track>` per file inside the `<video>`, and one control in `.luz-player-btns`. Use the button for one track and the select for several; the script fills the select.

Captions markup
```html
<video class="luz-player-video" preload="metadata" controls playsinline>
  <source src="interview.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  <track kind="captions" srclang="en" label="English" src="interview-en.vtt" default>
  <track kind="subtitles" srclang="es" label="Español" src="interview-es.vtt">
</video>

<!-- One track: a button that turns it on and off -->
<button class="luz-player-btn luz-player-captions" type="button" aria-pressed="false" aria-label="Captions">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" aria-hidden="true"><rect x="2" y="5" width="20" height="14" rx="2"/><path d="M6 11h12M6 15h7"/></svg>
</button>

<!-- Several tracks: a select, filled by the script -->
<select class="luz-input luz-player-tracks" aria-label="Captions"></select>
```

Player script code
```js
import { initPlayers } from "@luz-ds/core/player";
initPlayers();
```

### Variants and options
- `data-type="video"`: A `<video class="luz-player-video">`; a click on the picture plays or pauses
- `data-type="audio"`: An `<audio class="luz-player-audio">` with a compact control row (`.luz-player-controls--audio`)
- `data-type="midi"` and `data-src`: A MIDI file, played with Web Audio by `midi.js`, loaded only when needed
- `.luz-player-mute`, `.luz-player-volbar`: A mute button and a volume slider
- `.luz-player-fullscreen`, `.luz-player-pip`: Optional full-screen and picture-in-picture buttons for video
- `<track kind="captions">`, `kind="subtitles"`: A WebVTT file with `srclang` and `label`; `default` shows it from the start
- `.luz-player-captions`: A button that turns captions on and off: the default track, else the first
- `.luz-player-tracks`: A select, with `.luz-input`, to pick one track or none
- `.luz-player-fallback`: Text shown only when the script does not run

### How it works
The native media element plays the file; `player.js` drives the LUZ controls, styled by `components/player.css`.

- `initPlayers()` mounts every `.luz-player` on the page, or inside the element you pass it. `luz.js` runs it. A player already mounted is left as it is, so running it again is safe.
- On mount, the script removes the native `controls` and binds the LUZ ones: play and pause, time, seek and volume. They start from the media's own state: a `muted` video shows as muted, and a length the browser already knows shows at once.
- Seek and volume are native `<input type="range">` sliders. Once the length is known, the seek slider has one step per second, whatever its `max` in the markup.
- A full-screen or picture-in-picture button is hidden where the browser cannot do it.
- Captions and subtitles are the browser's: each `<track>` is a text track, and the browser draws its cues. The LUZ controls only set which track shows, so a choice made in the browser's own menu shows in them too. `::cue` gives the cues light text on the media surface. Nothing is stored. A control with no track to show is hidden.
- `mountPlayer(root)` and `mountMidiPlayer(root)` mount one player.
- The player is a size-query container: below 480 px of its own width the audio controls stack and the volume bar is hidden, wherever the player is placed. A parent that sizes it to its content (an inline-flex item, a float) needs a width of its own.
- In right-to-left text the timeline follows the reading direction: the seek bar starts at the right and fills towards the left, the controls row mirrors, and the slider's keys are the browser's own. The play, pause and volume icons are not mirrored: they do not point anywhere.

### Without JavaScript
Audio and video show the browser's own controls, and the LUZ controls stay hidden. The browser's controls offer the captions and subtitles, and a track with `default` shows from the start. A MIDI player shows its fallback text instead.

### Keyboard and ARIA
Tab moves through the controls; each one keeps its native keys.

- Buttons: Enter or Space. Their names change with the state: "Play" or "Pause", "Mute" or "Unmute". The captions button keeps its name, "Captions", and says whether it is pressed (`aria-pressed`).
- Track select: the browser's own keys; each option is in the language of its track.
- Sliders: arrow keys, Home, End, Page Up and Page Down. An arrow key moves the seek slider one second, and the volume slider one step (5 % in the example). The seek slider says the time as text.
- When the player itself has focus, not one of its controls (after a click on the video, for example): Space or K plays and pauses, and M mutes. F goes full screen and C turns captions on or off when the player has those buttons. With Ctrl, Alt or Cmd held, these keys do nothing.
- The player is a `role="group"` named by its `aria-label`.

### When to use
Use a player to play a video, a sound or a MIDI file inside the page, when the reader starts it.

### When not to use
Do not use a player for media that starts on its own or plays in the background.

- Never autoplay.
- For a short animated illustration with no sound, use an image or a [figure](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/figure/).

### Do and don't
- **Do** Controls the reader starts, and a name that says what plays. Shortened: the full markup is under Copy the markup.
- **Don't** Media that starts on its own. Sound that plays for more than 3 seconds must have a way to stop it (WCAG 1.4.2), so it is shown as code only.

### Writing the content
Name each player by what it plays: "Episode 12 player", not "Audio player".

- Give video captions (`<track kind="captions">`) and a transcript when it has speech. Captions include the sounds as well as the words; subtitles (`kind="subtitles"`) translate the words.
- Label each track in its own language: "English", "Español".
- Describe a silent video in its `aria-label` or next to it.
- Say the length and the format next to the player when it is large.

## Progress
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/progress/
Example: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/examples/components/progress.html
Files: components/progress.css · Package: @luz-ds/core

Shows how far a task that takes time has got, with the native progress element.

### Known issues
None known.

### Copy the markup
Progress bar with a visible label markup
```html
<label for="upload">Uploading report.pdf</label>
<progress class="luz-progress" id="upload" value="25" max="100">25%</progress>
```

### Variants and options
One class. The state comes from the native attributes.

- `value` and `max`: How much is done; `max` is 1 if you leave it out
- no `value`: Indeterminate: the task is running but its length is unknown

### How it works
The native `<progress>` element, styled by `components/progress.css`: an 8 px bar, full width, with the brand colour as the fill and a 1 px edge in the field border colour, so the whole length shows on any surface.

- The browser exposes the role and the value to assistive technology.
- In Chromium and WebKit browsers the fill slides to a new value; under reduced motion it jumps.
- In forced colors the bar keeps a border and draws the fill in the system highlight colour.

### Without JavaScript
The bar shows the value in the markup. Moving it needs your script, which sets `value`.

### Keyboard and ARIA
A progress bar is not interactive and takes no focus.

- Name it with a `<label>`, or an `aria-label` when no label is shown.
- Screen readers do not announce every change. Announce the start and the end in a polite live region (`role="status"`).

### When to use
Use a progress bar for a task that takes more than a few seconds, such as an upload or a build.

### When not to use
Do not use a progress bar for a value that is not a task.

- For a measure in a known range, such as storage used, use a [meter](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/meter/).
- Do not use it as decoration.

### Do and don't
- **Do** A task with an end, named with the figure: “Uploading report.pdf, 25%”.
- **Don't** Storage used is a measure, not a task: a progress bar suggests it will finish. Use a meter.

### Writing the content
Say what is happening, not just the number: "Uploading report.pdf".

- Put the figure in the name or next to the bar: "Upload, 25%".
- When it ends, say so: "Upload complete".

## Prose
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/prose/
Example: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/examples/components/prose.html
Files: components/prose.css · Package: @luz-ds/core

Sets long text in lines of about 70 characters, with space between its blocks, whatever markup an editor writes inside.

### Known issues
A table without a wrapper that is wider than the column pushes the page sideways on a narrow screen. Put a wide table in core's [table](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/table/) wrapper, `.luz-table-wrap`, which scrolls inside itself. Not yet tested with a screen reader.

### Copy the markup
Prose markup
```html
<div class="luz-prose">
  <!-- What the editor or the Markdown writes, as it is -->
  <p>Since March 2016, a group of volunteers has read the tide gauge…</p>
  <h2 id="method">How the readings were taken</h2>
  <p>…</p>
  <ul class="wp-block-list">
    <li>…</li>
  </ul>
  <figure>
    <img src="gauge.jpg" width="1200" height="800" alt="The tide gauge in the port, a post marked in centimetres">
    <figcaption>The gauge at low tide.</figcaption>
  </figure>
</div>
```

### Variants and options
There are no modifiers.

- `.luz-prose`: On the element that holds the text: lines of about 70 characters, the space between its blocks, the indent and markers of its lists, inline code as a chip
- `--luz-prose-measure`: The longest line, `70ch` by default. Set it on the wrapper, between `60ch` and `80ch`
- `data-luz-classless` on the same element: With [classless mode](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/classless/) loaded, its tables, buttons and fields take the look of core's components

### How it works
CSS only, in `components/prose.css`. Every selector is inside `:where()`, so a LUZ component inside the text, or a rule of yours, wins.

- **Line length.** Each block of the wrapper is at most `--luz-prose-measure` wide. Figures, tables, code blocks, images, videos and `.luz-table-wrap` take the whole width of the wrapper, never more.
- **Space between blocks.** A block starts `--luz-space-md` below the one before it. A heading or a rule starts further down (`--luz-space-xl`), and the block after a heading sits closer (`--luz-space-sm`). Margins, not a gap: a component inside keeps its own margin, and the two collapse.
- **Lists.** Every list gets its indent and markers back, with a class or without one (an editor's `ul.wp-block-list`), except a list with a layout object (`.o-grid`, `.o-stack`) or a LUZ component class.
- **Inline code** has the look of `.luz-code-inline`. Long words and addresses break rather than push the page sideways.
- **Classless mode** takes the same three steps between blocks, so the two agree; prose is in a later layer, so it wins where they meet. Prose adds the line length and the lists; classless mode adds the look of tables and controls.

### Without JavaScript
Nothing changes: prose is CSS.

### Keyboard and ARIA
Prose takes no focus and adds no role. Tab reaches the links and controls inside it, in source order.

- A long `<pre>` scrolls sideways inside itself. To scroll it with the keyboard, give it `tabindex="0"`, `role="region"` and a name, as core's [code block](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/code/) does.
- The headings inside make the outline of the text: start at the level under the page's title, and do not skip one.

### When to use
Use prose around running text whose markup you do not write block by block: the body of a post or a page from a CMS editor, Markdown, a help article.

### When not to use
Do not put prose around a whole page or an interface: the header, the navigation, forms and cards lay themselves out.

- For a column of blocks you build yourself, use [`.o-stack`](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/layout/).
- For one or two lines inside a component, such as a card's text, use the component's own classes.

### Do and don't
- **Do** Short paragraphs under headings that say what follows, so a reader can scan and find their place.
- **Don't** One long paragraph with no heading: the reader cannot tell what it covers without reading all of it.

### Writing the content
Write for someone who reads the first words of each line and skips the rest.

- One idea a paragraph. Put the point first.
- Headings in order, in sentence case, that say what the section is about.
- A list for three or more things of the same kind; a sentence for two.
- Links that say where they go, and figures with a caption that says what they show.

## Select
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/select/
Example: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/examples/components/select.html
Files: components/select.css · Package: @luz-ds/core

A native drop-down list for choosing one option from a long list, with the closed box styled by tokens.

### Known issues
The open list looks different in each browser and system. This is intended.

- The closed box is the same everywhere. The list that opens from it is drawn by the browser or the operating system, and it is the one the reader already knows.
- Browsers that support `appearance: base-select` (Chrome and Edge 135 and later, Safari 27 and later) also get the list in LUZ's colors, shape and spacing. Firefox shows its own list.
- On phones, the system's own picker opens, and LUZ cannot style it.

### Copy the markup
Select markup
```html
<div class="luz-field">
  <label class="luz-field__label" for="country">Country</label>
  <select class="luz-select" id="country" name="country">
    <option value="">Select a country</option>
    <option value="de">Germany</option>
    <option value="es">Spain</option>
    <option value="fr">France</option>
  </select>
</div>
```

### Variants and options
One class, on the `<select>` itself. There is no wrapper and no modifier: the state comes from the native attributes.

- `.luz-select`: The closed box: 44 px high, a bottom border and an arrow at the end of the line
- `aria-invalid="true"`: The error state: a thicker border in the danger color. Pair it with the error text
- `disabled`: Disabled text and a dashed border
- `multiple`, `size`: A list that stays open, with a full border and no arrow
- `<optgroup label>`: A labelled set of options

### How it works
A native `<select>` styled by `components/select.css`, in two layers. No JavaScript.

- **The closed box, in every browser.** Border, height, type and colors come from tokens. The arrow is two gradients in `currentcolor`, so it follows the text color, the disabled state and forced colors. It sits at the inline end, so it moves to the left in right-to-left text.
- **The open list, where the browser can.** Inside `@supports (appearance: base-select)` the list, its options and the check mark are styled too. Outside it nothing changes.
- `color-scheme` follows the color mode, so the system's own list opens in the right mode.

### Without JavaScript
Nothing changes: the select is a native element and LUZ adds no script to it.

### Keyboard and ARIA
The native keys apply, and which ones open the list differs a little between systems.

- Tab moves to the select. Enter or Space opens the list, and Escape closes it without a change.
- Up and Down move through the options, and typing the first letters jumps to a match.
- Give it a visible `<label for>`. Add no role: the element already has its semantics.
- For an error, set `aria-invalid="true"` and point `aria-describedby` at the error text.

### When to use
Use a select when the reader must choose one option from a long list they already know the answer to.

- A country, a year, a time zone: more than six options, one answer.
- The options are short and the reader can scan them in order.

### When not to use
A select hides the options until the reader opens it, and some people find that hard. The [GOV.UK Design System](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/select/) says to use it as a last resort. The rule of six is LUZ's own: that guide gives no number.

- With six options or fewer, use [radio buttons](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/form/): every option stays in view.
- To choose several, use [checkboxes](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/form/).
- Before you use a long list, ask a question that cuts it down.
- Never build your own listbox from `<div>` elements, or hide the select behind a copy of it.

### Do and don't
- **Do** Use a select for a long list, with a visible label that says what to choose.
- **Don't** Hide three options in a select. Radio buttons show them all at once.

### Writing the content
- The label says what to choose, as a noun: "Country", not "Please select".
- The first option is a prompt such as "Select a country", with an empty value, so a required field is not answered by default.
- Write each option in sentence case and put them in an order the reader can predict, such as alphabetical.
- Give every option text. An icon or a color swatch can go with it, never instead of it.

## Sidebar
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/sidebar/
Example: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/examples/components/sidebar.html
Files: components/sidebar.css · Package: @luz-ds/core

Holds the main navigation of a site or an app, and becomes a drawer on small screens.

### Known issues
In a browser without the popover API the navigation does not become a drawer: it stays visible above the content on small screens.

### Copy the markup
Sidebar with its drawer button markup
```html
<header>
  <button class="luz-nav-toggle" type="button" popovertarget="site-nav" aria-label="Menu">
    <span class="luz-nav-toggle__bar"></span>
    <span class="luz-nav-toggle__bar"></span>
    <span class="luz-nav-toggle__bar"></span>
  </button>
</header>

<nav class="luz-sidebar" id="site-nav" popover aria-label="Main">
  <div class="luz-sidebar__section">
    <div class="luz-sidebar__section-label">Account</div>
    <a class="luz-sidebar__link is-active" href="/profile/" aria-current="page">Profile</a>
    <a class="luz-sidebar__link" href="/billing/">Billing</a>
  </div>
</nav>
```

Sidebar script code
```js
import { initSidebar } from "@luz-ds/core/sidebar";
initSidebar();
```

### Variants and options
- `.luz-sidebar`: The navigation column, in the sidebar colours
- `popover` on `.luz-sidebar`: Makes it a drawer at 768 px and below
- `.luz-sidebar__brand`, `__brand-name`, `__logo`, `__version`: An optional brand block at the top
- `.luz-sidebar__section`, `__section-label`: A group of links and its label
- `.luz-sidebar__link`: A link
- `data-luz-spy` on any element: Not part of the sidebar: the scroll spy also marks the links to sections of the page inside it, such as a table of contents styled your own way
- `.is-active` on a link: Marks the current link with weight and colour; pair it with `aria-current="page"`
- `.luz-sidebar__footer`: Pinned to the bottom, for example for the [color mode switcher](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/mode-switcher/)
- `.luz-nav-toggle`: The menu button, shown at 768 px and below; put it first in your header row
- `.luz-nav-toggle--fixed`: Pins the menu button to the top start corner, for a page with no header

### How it works
A `<nav>` landmark, styled by `components/sidebar.css`. On small screens it is a native popover drawer.

- The menu button opens it with `popovertarget`, with no script. The browser gives Escape, a click outside to close, the top layer and the expanded state.
- `initSidebar()` from `sidebar.js` is optional: it marks the link of the section in view on a long page (`aria-current="true"`) and closes the drawer when a link is followed. `luz.js` runs it.
- The scroll spy finds its links by `.luz-sidebar__link`, and by `data-luz-spy`: on any element (a `<nav>` of contents), it spies every link inside that points at a section of the page (`href="#…"`). The attribute is the hook; the look of those links is yours.

### Without JavaScript
The sidebar and the drawer work. The current link is the one your markup marks; it does not follow the scroll.

### Keyboard and ARIA
Tab moves through the links in order. On small screens, the menu button opens the drawer; Escape or a click outside closes it, and focus goes back to the button.

- Name the `<nav>` with `aria-label` when the page has more than one.
- Mark the current page with `aria-current="page"` as well as `.is-active`: the class is only the look.
- The menu button keeps the name "Menu" whether the drawer is open or closed; the popover exposes the state.

### When to use
Use a sidebar for the main navigation of an app or a documentation site with many sections.

### When not to use
Do not use a sidebar for a site with a few pages: a header navigation is simpler.

- For the trail to the current page, use a [breadcrumb](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/breadcrumb/).
- For panels of one page, use [tabs](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/tabs/).

### Do and don't
- **Do** Short nouns, grouped under a label, in the order people need them.
- **Don't** Sentences and catch-alls as links: “Manage your billing details” is slow to scan and “Other stuff” says nothing.

### Writing the content
Name each link after the page it opens, in a word or two.

- Section labels are nouns: "Account", "Billing".
- Order the links by how often people need them.

## Skip link
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/skip-link/
Example: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/examples/components/skip-link.html
Files: components/skip-link.css · Package: @luz-ds/core

Lets keyboard users jump past the header to the main content.

### Known issues
None known.

### Copy the markup
Skip link markup
```html
<body>
  <a class="luz-skip-link" href="#main-content">Skip to main content</a>
  <header class="o-sticky">…</header>
  <main id="main-content" tabindex="-1">…</main>
</body>
```

### Variants and options
There are no variants: one class on one link.

- `.luz-skip-link`: Off screen until it has focus, then fixed at the top start corner, in the brand fill, above everything, a sticky bar included. Not printed

### How it works
A normal link to the `id` of `<main>`, first in `<body>`, before a cookie banner, a notice or the header. CSS only.

- It slides in when it receives focus, over `--luz-duration-fast`; under reduced motion it appears at once.
- The browser does the jump. `tabindex="-1"` on `<main>` lets it take the focus, so the next Tab starts inside it in every browser.
- Under a sticky bar ([.o-sticky](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/layout/#objects-page)) the page's scroll padding keeps the start of `<main>` below the bar after the jump.

### Without JavaScript
Nothing changes: the skip link is a link and CSS.

### Keyboard and ARIA
Press Tab once from the top of the page and the link appears; Enter follows it to the main content.

- It must be the first focusable element of the page, before a cookie banner or a notice.
- No ARIA: its text is its name.

### When to use
Put a skip link on every page that has a header, a banner or navigation before the main content.

### When not to use
Do not rely on it alone: the page still needs landmarks and a logical heading order.

- Do not add a list of skip links to every section: one to the main content is enough.

### Do and don't
- **Do** One link, that says where it goes: “Skip to main content”.
- **Don't** A row of skip links: the reader has to read them all before the page starts, which is what the link was meant to avoid.

### Writing the content
Say where it goes: "Skip to main content".

- Use the same text on every page.

## Table
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/table/
Example: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/examples/components/table.html
Files: components/table.css · Package: @luz-ds/core

Compares records across several attributes, in rows and columns that stay readable at 320 px.

### Known issues
Sorting in the browser (`data-luz-sort`) is checked in the Chromium accessibility tree only, and not yet tested with NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, TalkBack or Orca. The sorted column is exposed with `aria-sort` on its column header and each sort is announced in a status message; tabbing through the headings announces the column name, and the sort state is read on the header cell and in the status message.

- Only the rows loaded in the page are sorted, the sort is not remembered on reload, and the address bar does not change. A table with several header rows or a `colspan` heading is not supported, and anything in a sortable heading besides its text or one link is dropped when it becomes a button.
- Sorting a few thousand rows moves them all in one task: sort them on the server. The order of text depends on the browser's collation for the language of the table.

### Copy the markup
Table markup
```html
<div class="luz-table-wrap" role="region" aria-label="Invoices" tabindex="0">
  <table class="luz-table">
    <caption>Invoices</caption>
    <thead>
      <tr><th scope="col">Number</th><th scope="col">Date</th><th scope="col">Amount (€)</th></tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr><td data-label="Number">INV-0042</td><td data-label="Date">1 Oct 2026</td><td data-label="Amount (€)">120.00</td></tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
</div>
```

### Variants and options
- `.luz-table`: Full width, header row on the strong surface, a rule between rows, a highlight on the row under the pointer
- `.luz-table-wrap`: Scrolls the table sideways when it is wider than its container
- `.luz-table--sticky-col`: Keeps the first column in view while the table scrolls sideways
- `.luz-table--compact`: Less space above and below each row (about 33 px for a line of text, not 49 px) and a narrower gutter between columns; the type size does not change
- `.luz-table__numeric` on a `<th>` and its `<td>`: Aligns a column of numbers to the end of the cell, in figures of equal width
- `data-luz-sort` on a `<th scope="col">`: The column can be sorted in the browser: its text becomes a button
- `data-sort-value` on a `<td>`: What the cell sorts by when its text is not that: a formatted number (`1,204`), a date shown as “13 Oct”, a price with its currency
- `aria-sort` on the sorted `<th>`: `ascending` or `descending`, on one heading only: a triangle shows the direction
- `data-label` on each `<td>`: The column name shown before the value when rows become cards

Numbers and dense data take a class each. Put the numeric class on the heading as well as on every cell of the column.

#### Sorting in the browser

Mark each sortable heading with `data-luz-sort`. The script turns its text into a button; the table keeps working without it.

Sortable table markup
```html
<table class="luz-table" id="routes">
  <caption>Parcels per route</caption>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <!-- With a link: it sorts on the server without JavaScript -->
      <th scope="col" data-luz-sort><a href="?sort=route#routes">Route</a></th>
      <!-- Plain text: the script makes it a button -->
      <th scope="col" class="luz-table__numeric" data-luz-sort>Parcels</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td data-label="Route">Sevilla to Madrid</td>
      <td class="luz-table__numeric" data-label="Parcels" data-sort-value="1204">1,204</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

- **The cell's text is what it sorts by,** unless it has `data-sort-value`. Two plain numbers (`12`, `0.5`, `-3`) sort as numbers; anything else sorts as text, in the order of the table's language, with `Room 2` before `Room 10`.
- **A number with a thousands separator, a unit or a currency needs `data-sort-value`** with the plain number (`1204` for `1,204`), or it sorts as text and “1,204” falls before “999”. A date is an ISO date (`2026-10-13`), whatever it shows.
- **Equal values keep their order.** The first press sorts ascending, the next descending, and so on; to go back to the first order, reload.
- **The heading says the column and nothing else.** No direction in its text and none in the caption: the triangle, `aria-sort` and the status line say it, and they follow the sort.

### How it works
A native `<table>` with `<caption>`, `<thead>` and `<th scope>`, styled by `components/table.css`. No JavaScript.

- The wrapper is a container: below 480 px of its own width, a container query turns each row into a card of label and value pairs and reduces the cell padding. It follows the width of the wrapper, not the window, so a narrow table in a wide page stacks too.
- The labels come from `data-label`; a cell without one shows its value only.
- A cell that holds more than one element needs a wrapper `<div>` inside it, so the value stays together.
- `.luz-table__numeric` sets `text-align: end` and `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, so the digits of a column line up whatever the language. In the stacked card layout the value is already at the end of its row.
- `.luz-table--compact` changes only the padding of the cells: the type keeps its size, so the table is denser but no harder to read.
- **Sorted by the server**, for paginated or filtered results and for every table without JavaScript: each heading is a link to the same page sorted by that column, and only the sorted column's `<th scope="col">` carries `aria-sort="ascending"` or `"descending"`. Say the direction in the visible text of the link too, for example “Amount (€), ascending”; make the link's text start with the heading's own words; end its `href` with the table's `id` (`?sort=amount&dir=desc#invoices`) so the next Tab starts at the table after the page reloads; and state the sort in the caption (“Invoices, sorted by amount, ascending”).
- **Sorted in the browser**, for a table that holds all its rows: `data-luz-sort` on the headings. `luz.js` loads `table-sort.js` on demand, only on a page that has such a heading, and each heading's text (or the content of its link) moves into a `<button type="button">`. A press sorts every `<tbody>` in place, writes `aria-sort` on that heading alone and says “Sorted by Parcels, ascending” in an `<output>` that reads politely and is hidden visually. Focus stays on the button. A table that sorts in the browser has no direction in its caption or headings: they would be wrong after one press.
- The triangle after the sorted heading is drawn by CSS from `aria-sort` (a shape, not text), so a server-sorted heading gets it too. Up is ascending, down is descending.
- Below 480 px a heading row that holds a link or a button stays visible: its headings show as a row above the cards, and wrap, so the controls can be seen and reached. A heading row of plain text is hidden there, as before, because each card carries its labels.
- Cards change the `display` of the table elements, which can hide the table from some screen readers. The stylesheet recommends `role="table"`, `"row"` and `"cell"` on a table that stacks.

### Without JavaScript
Nothing changes: scrolling, the sticky column and the cards are all CSS. A heading with a link sorts on the server; a plain heading is just a heading. Rows are never hidden, and if the script does not load the table stays whole.

#### Loading the sort on its own

The module has no imports and no effect until you call it. Pass the `t` of core's strings so the status line is written in the table's language; without it the table still sorts and the status line stays empty.

Table sort code
```js
import { initTableSort } from "@luz-ds/core/table-sort";
import { t } from "@luz-ds/core/i18n";

initTableSort(document, t);
```

### Keyboard and ARIA
The wrapper takes focus (`tabindex="0"`) so keyboard users can scroll it with the arrow keys.

- Give the wrapper `role="region"` and an `aria-label`, so that focus stop has a name.
- `scope="col"` on column headers, and `scope="row"` on a header cell that names its row.
- A sortable heading is a button: Tab reaches it, Enter or Space sorts, and focus stays on it while the rows move. A link that the script replaces keeps the focus it had.
- `aria-sort` is on the one sorted `<th scope="col">`. Each sort is announced by the status line (`<output>`, role `status`), in the language of the table; the strings are `sortedAsc` and `sortedDesc` of core's strings (see [JavaScript modules](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/get-started/javascript/); `data-luz-label-sorted-asc` and `data-luz-label-sorted-desc` override them).
- The column name is the heading's text only: no arrow character, no “ascending” in the markup.

### When to use
Use a table to compare records across the same attributes: services and their status, invoices and their amounts.

### When not to use
Do not use a table for layout.

- For one attribute per item, use a list.
- For a few items of equal weight, use [cards](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/card/).
- For a data grid (filters, selecting rows, editing cells or thousands of rows), use a library built for it. LUZ's table shows rows and sorts them; it does not manage them. For paginated results, sort on the server.
- For a trend over time, use a chart library and keep the table as its text alternative. A bar for each row is a [meter](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/meter/) in the cell of its figure.

### Do and don't
- **Do** The unit in the heading, the same decimals, and the column aligned to the end, heading included.
- **Don't** A vague heading, the unit in every cell, mixed decimals and no alignment: the column is hard to compare.

### Writing the content
The caption names the table; column headings are short nouns.

- Put units in the heading, not in every cell: "Amount (€)".
- Put the column that identifies the row first.
- Align numbers to the end with `.luz-table__numeric`, on the heading and on every cell of the column, with the same number of decimals. Text stays at the start.
- In a table that sorts in the browser, the heading is the column name and its unit, “Weight (kg)”: no arrow and no direction, in the heading or in the caption.

## Tabs
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/tabs/
Example: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/examples/components/tabs.html
Files: components/tabs.css · Package: @luz-ds/core

Switches between panels of related content in one place; without JavaScript the panels are stacked sections.

### Known issues
None known.

### Copy the markup
Tabs markup
```html
<nav class="luz-tabs" aria-label="Project">
  <a class="luz-tab" href="#project-summary">Summary</a>
  <a class="luz-tab" href="#project-settings">Settings</a>
</nav>
<div class="luz-tabpanel" id="project-summary">…</div>
<div class="luz-tabpanel" id="project-settings">…</div>
```

Tabs script code
```js
import { initTabs } from "@luz-ds/core/tabs";
initTabs();
```

### Variants and options
One look. The tab that opens first is the first one that matches:

- 1: The tab whose panel holds the element named in the URL fragment
- 2: A tab with `aria-selected="true"` or `.is-active` in the markup
- 3: The first tab

### How it works
A row of in-page links to the panels, styled by `components/tabs.css` and upgraded by `tabs.js`.

- `initTabs()` adds the ARIA tabs pattern: `role="tablist"`, `"tab"` and `"tabpanel"`, `aria-selected`, `aria-controls`, `aria-labelledby` and a roving `tabindex`. It hides the inactive panels. `luz.js` runs it.
- A link to an element inside a hidden panel opens its tab, on load, on `hashchange` and on click.
- Inactive panels are `hidden="until-found"` where the browser supports it, so find in page reaches them and opens their tab.
- `activateTab(tab)` selects a tab from your own script.

### Without JavaScript
The tabs are a row of links, and every panel is shown, stacked, in order. Each link jumps to its panel. Give each panel a heading, so the stacked page still reads well.

### Keyboard and ARIA
Tab moves into the tab row, to the selected tab; Tab again leaves for the panel.

- Left and Right (or Up and Down) move to the next tab and select it; Home and End go to the first and the last.
- Space or Enter selects the focused tab.
- In right-to-left text, Left and Right follow the reading direction.
- Name the tab row with `aria-label`; the name stays when it becomes a tab list.

### When to use
Use tabs to switch between panels of the same level that readers do not need side by side, such as the summary, settings and logs of one service.

### When not to use
Do not use tabs to move between pages, or to hide content readers need all at once.

- Between pages, use a [sidebar](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/sidebar/) or header links.
- For steps in order, use separate pages.
- More than five or six tabs do not fit a phone: use sections with headings.

### Do and don't
- **Do** Tabs named after their panels, in a word or two.
- **Don't** Numbered steps as tabs: a process in order belongs on separate pages, and nothing stops the reader from skipping a step.

### Writing the content
Name each tab after its panel, in one or two words.

- Sentence case, no verbs: "Summary", "Settings".
- Use the same name for the panel's heading.

## Tag and badge
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/tag/
Example: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/examples/components/tag.html
Files: components/tag.css · Package: @luz-ds/core

Labels an item with a short status or category (tag), or shows a count (badge).

### Known issues
None known.

### Copy the markup
Status tag markup
```html
<span class="luz-tag luz-tag--green luz-tag--dot">Running</span>
```

Count badge markup
```html
<a href="/inbox/">Inbox <span class="luz-badge luz-badge--primary">3</span><span class="u-sr-only"> unread</span></a>
```

### Variants and options
A tag takes one colour and, if you like, the dot. A badge takes one colour.

- `.luz-tag--gray`: Neutral: a category with no status
- `.luz-tag--blue`: Information colours
- `.luz-tag--green`: Success colours
- `.luz-tag--yellow`: Warning colours
- `.luz-tag--red`: Danger colours
- `.luz-tag--teal`, `.luz-tag--purple`: Extra colours for categories, with no status meaning
- `.luz-tag--dot`: A small dot before the text, a second cue besides colour
- `.luz-badge--primary`: Brand fill
- `.luz-badge--gray`: Neutral fill
- `.luz-badge--danger`: Danger fill

### How it works
Inline `<span>` elements, styled by `components/tag.css`. No JavaScript.

- A tag is at least 24 px high, in extra-small text, on a tint of its colour.
- A badge is a small rounded count in the mono font, at least 20 px wide.

### Without JavaScript
Nothing changes: tags and badges are HTML and CSS.

### Keyboard and ARIA
Tags and badges are not interactive and take no focus.

- The text carries the meaning; the colour adds nothing a screen reader needs.
- A count needs context: put the badge inside the link or heading it counts, and add the unit as visually hidden text if it is not on screen ("3 unread").

### When to use
Use a tag to label an item with a short status or category, and a badge to show a count next to a link or a heading.

### When not to use
Do not use a tag for an action: it is not clickable.

- For an action, use a [button](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/button/).
- For a sentence, use an [alert](https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/alert/).
- Do not give teal or purple a status meaning: they are for categories.

### Do and don't
- **Do** Status colours for status: green running, yellow degraded, red stopped, each with its word.
- **Don't** Teal and purple as statuses: they are for categories, so the reader cannot guess that teal means running.

### Writing the content
One or two words, in sentence case: "Running", "Degraded".

- Never only a colour name: the reader may not see the colour.
- Badges hold numbers; cap them ("99+") so they keep their size.

## Timeline
URL: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/docs/components/timeline/
Example: https://nandovejer.github.io/luz/examples/components/timeline.html
Files: components/timeline.css · Package: @luz-ds/core

Shows dated events in order, one card at a time on a rail of dates or all at once down a line; without JavaScript it is a list.

### Known issues
Three things are not done yet, and none has been tested with a screen reader.

- The Previous and Next buttons are named only "Previous" and "Next". The name does not say which date they lead to.
- Whether a screen reader announces the card that appears when you change the item has not been tested.
- The timeline has not been tested with any screen reader: no result is claimed for NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, TalkBack or Orca.

### Copy the markup
An ordered list inside `<luz-timeline>`. Give the element `role="group"` and a name with `aria-label`, so the name is read without JavaScript too.

Timeline markup
```html
<luz-timeline role="group" aria-label="Releases of the app">
  <ol class="luz-timeline">
    <li class="luz-timeline__item">
      <time class="luz-timeline__date" datetime="2025-03">March 2025</time>
      <p class="luz-timeline__title">First beta</p>
      <p class="luz-timeline__text">Ten teams try the app.</p>
    </li>
    <li class="luz-timeline__item">
      <time class="luz-timeline__date" datetime="2025-06">June 2025</time>
      <p class="luz-timeline__title">Public launch</p>
      <p class="luz-timeline__text">Sign-up opens to everyone.</p>
    </li>
  </ol>
</luz-timeline>
```

With autoplay, every four seconds:

Timeline with autoplay markup
```html
<luz-timeline role="group" aria-label="Milestones" autoplay interval="4000">
  <ol class="luz-timeline">
    <li class="luz-timeline__item">
      <time class="luz-timeline__date" datetime="2023">2023</time>
      <p class="luz-timeline__title">The idea</p>
      <p class="luz-timeline__text">Two people sketch the first screens.</p>
    </li>
    <li class="luz-timeline__item">
      <time class="luz-timeline__date" datetime="2024">2024</time>
      <p class="luz-timeline__title">The team</p>
      <p class="luz-timeline__text">Five people work on it full time.</p>
    </li>
    <li class="luz-timeline__item">
      <time class="luz-timeline__date" datetime="2025">2025</time>
      <p class="luz-timeline__title">The first customers</p>
      <p class="luz-timeline__text">Fifty schools use it every week.</p>
    </li>
  </ol>
</luz-timeline>
```

The vertical layout:

Vertical timeline markup
